title: Tools and guards: MCP and hooks (Claude Code), OpenCode equivalents
text:
Checked 2026-11-16. Official docs only. Pages fetched via a summarising fetch tool (quotes as returned; long pages read in chunks, saved locally and grepped). No model-calling commands were run. Base: C = https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ ; O = https://opencode.ai/docs/ Note: the OpenCode docs now describe “V2” (docker tag 2.0.0, /v2/install). V1 key names differ (see section A4). Verify against the user’s installed version.



CONFIRMED: HTTP (recommended): claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>. C mcp
CONFIRMED: SSE is deprecated: “The SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport is deprecated. Use HTTP servers instead, where available.” claude mcp add --transport sse <name> <url>. C mcp
CONFIRMED: stdio: claude mcp add [options] <name> -- <command> [args...]. “Everything after -- is passed to the server untouched.” Flags: -s/--scope, -e/--env KEY=value, -t/--transport, -H/--header. C mcp
CONFIRMED: project file .mcp.json at the project root: { "mcpServers": { "shared-server": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/mcp" } } } C mcp
UNCONFIRMED: exact .mcp.json shape for a stdio server (command/args/env keys not seen in the fetched text). Check C mcp before putting it in a quest.
CONFIRMED: /mcp inside a session lists servers and tools (page refers to running /mcp). C mcp





CONFIRMED scopes: Local (default; current project only; not shared; stored in ~/.claude.json), Project (shared via version control; .mcp.json in project root), User (all your projects; ~/.claude.json). C mcp
CONFIRMED: “Local scope is the default.”
CONFIRMED: “For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval in interactive sessions before using project-scoped servers from .mcp.json files. To reset those approval choices, run claude mcp reset-project-choices.” C mcp
CONFIRMED: in claude -p and Agent SDK runs “Claude Code can’t show that prompt: it loads project-scoped servers without asking.” Mitigations named: disabledMcpjsonServers, --setting-sources/settingSources, --strict-mcp-config. C mcp
Teaching point: a cloned repo’s .mcp.json is code that wants to run on your machine; the approval prompt is the gate, and headless mode has no gate.





CONFIRMED naming: mcp__<server>__<tool>. “To match every tool from an MCP server, write mcp__<server>__*. To match one tool, write its full name.” C permissions
CONFIRMED examples: mcp__puppeteer (any tool of the server), mcp__puppeteer__*, mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate (one tool). C permissions
CONFIRMED: characters such as . or spaces in server names become _ (my.server -> mcp__my_server__*). C permissions
CONFIRMED: allow-rule globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix; “An unanchored allow glob such as "*", "B*", or "mcp__*" is skipped and doesn’t auto-approve anything.” Deny/ask accept "mcp__*" (every MCP tool, all servers). C permissions
CONFIRMED: parameter matching: “When Claude Code loads a settings file, it skips any mcp__ rule that has parentheses.” Parameter-level deny for MCP only via --disallowedTools. C permissions
CONFIRMED: deny and ask rules are evaluated even when a hook returns allow (hooks page). C hooks
Minimal settings sketch (shape from the permissions page; check that page for allow/deny array syntax before quoting): "permissions": { "allow": ["mcp__github__get_*"], "deny": ["mcp__github__delete_*"] }. The allow/deny key names are UNCONFIRMED in the text fetched for this note.





CONFIRMED capabilities listed: implement features from issue trackers, analyze monitoring data, query databases, integrate designs, automate workflows, react to external events. C mcp
CONFIRMED security warning (the only one found): “Verify you trust each server before connecting it. Servers that fetch external content can expose you to prompt injection risk.” C mcp
UNCONFIRMED: any longer docs passage on injection via tool results (page text read in full except possibly a few chunks; nothing else found). Do not attribute more to the docs than the sentence above.
UNCONFIRMED as docs wording: “a stdio server runs code on your machine with your credentials”. The docs show stdio servers are commands Claude Code launches (-- <command>), and -e KEY=value passes secrets to them; the credentials statement is inference, label it so.
CONFIRMED org controls exist: allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers, managed-mcp.json. C mcp, C managed-mcp (linked)
CONFIRMED: sandboxing note, “sandbox restrictions still apply even if a prompt injection bypasses Claude’s decision-making” (use sandbox plus permissions). C permissions





CONFIRMED (V2): servers go “under mcp.servers”; “V2 does not place server names directly under mcp.” O mcp-servers
CONFIRMED local shape: "type": "local", "command": ["npx","-y","example-mcp-server"], "environment": {...}, "cwd": ".". O mcp-servers
CONFIRMED remote shape: "type": "remote", "url", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:MCP_API_KEY}" }, "oauth": false. O mcp-servers
CONFIRMED: disable via "disabled": true (no enabled field documented in V2). O mcp-servers
CONFIRMED: “MCP tools consume model context, so add only the servers you need.” O mcp-servers
CONFIRMED permissions: rules are an ordered array "permissions": [ { "action", "resource", "effect" } ], effect allow|ask|deny; last matching rule wins; no match means ask. MCP tool action is <server>_<tool> with resource * (unsupported chars become _); example { "action": "context7_*", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }. O permissions, O mcp-servers
CONFIRMED: V2 names are permissions/shell/subagent, replacing V1 permission/bash/task. O permissions
UNCONFIRMED: V1 mcp key shape (V1 docs not fetched).





CONFIRMED locations: ~/.claude/settings.json (all projects), .claude/settings.json (project, committable), .claude/settings.local.json (project, not shared), managed policy settings, plugin hooks/hooks.json; skill/subagent frontmatter also define hooks. C hooks
CONFIRMED: “To create a hook, add a hooks block to a settings file.” C hooks-guide
CONFIRMED matcher syntax: only letters, digits, _, -, spaces, ,, | means exact string or list; any other character means a JavaScript regex, unanchored. Edit|Write is a list; ^Notebook is a regex. C hooks
CONFIRMED MCP matching: mcp__<server>__<tool>; “The .* is required: a matcher like mcp__memory … is compared as an exact string and matches no tool.” Use mcp__memory__.*. C hooks
CONFIRMED input: JSON on stdin with session_id, cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input (Bash: tool_input.command), tool_use_id. C hooks




Config (.claude/settings.json; shape from the hooks docs example, matcher: "Bash", command path via $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR):
{ "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash",
  "hooks": [ { "type": "command",
    "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/block-drop-table.sh" } ] } ] } }
Script (verbatim from C hooks-guide, “Hook output”), chmod +x needed (UNCONFIRMED in docs text read; standard for executables):
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command')
if echo "$COMMAND" | grep -q "drop table"; then
  echo "Blocked: dropping tables is not allowed" >&2  # stderr becomes Claude's feedback
  exit 2                                               # exit 2 = block the action
fi
exit 0  # exit 0 = no decision; the normal permission flow applies

CONFIRMED: exit 2 on PreToolUse “Blocks the tool call”; “Claude sees the stderr message as the denial reason.” C hooks
CONFIRMED: exit 0 does not approve: “the tool call still goes through the normal permission flow”. C hooks-guide
CONFIRMED: any other exit code with no valid JSON: “the action proceeds on most events” (a hook that crashes fails open), unless the hook is configured to block on failure (onFailure: "block"). C hooks-guide
CONFIRMED JSON alternative: exit 0 and print to stdout: {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Destructive command blocked by hook"}}. Values allow|deny|ask|defer. “Choose one approach per hook” (exit 2 or JSON, not both). C hooks, C hooks-guide
CONFIRMED: precedence across hooks deny > defer > ask > allow; all matching hooks run to completion (a deny does not stop a sibling hook’s side effects). "allow" skips the prompt but “Deny and ask rules are still evaluated regardless of what the hook returns”. C hooks





CONFIRMED: exit 2 on PostToolUse “Shows stderr to Claude; the tool already ran”. Cannot block. C hooks
CONFIRMED example: matcher Edit|Write, command f=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path') && npx prettier --write --ignore-unknown "$f". C hooks-guide
CONFIRMED: updatedToolOutput “only changes what Claude sees. The tool has already run by the time the hook fires, so any files written, commands executed, or network requests sent have already taken effect.” C hooks





CONFIRMED: “Command hooks execute shell commands with your full user permissions. They can modify, delete, or access any files your user account can access. Review and test all hook commands before adding them to your configuration.” C hooks (Security considerations)
CONFIRMED: interactive sessions hold back hooks from every settings file until you accept the workspace trust dialog. In -p/SDK sessions “Claude Code never shows the dialog and treats the folder as trusted, so hooks committed in a repository’s .claude/settings.json run in a folder you’ve never trusted.” Advice: review .claude/ first, use --bare, or --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'. C hooks
CONFIRMED: best practices: validate inputs, quote variables, block .. path traversal, absolute paths, skip .env/.git/keys. C hooks
CONFIRMED limits: PreToolUse fires only when Claude calls a tool; @-referenced files in a prompt are added without a tool call so no hook (even Read) fires; none for EndConversation. Setup hooks cannot block. UserPromptSubmit cannot replace the prompt. C hooks
CONFIRMED: a matcher is a filter on tool name, not on content: a grep on tool_input.command sees only the literal string (our inference: it will miss rm hidden in a script the command runs; label as inference when teaching).
CONFIRMED: sandbox is an OS-enforced boundary for shell commands only and is off by default; file tools, MCP servers and hooks run outside it; it is one layer. Source: research/kennel-and-crypt.md, “Sandbox” section (lines 80-86). Argument-pattern deny rules are fragile: research/kennel-and-crypt.md line 219.
UNCONFIRMED: statement that a Bash-pattern hook can be evaded by obfuscation; not in the docs text read.





CONFIRMED (V2): plugins add “tools, hooks, integrations, commands, agents”. O plugins, O build/plugins
CONFIRMED locations: .opencode/plugins/ (project) and ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ (global); direct .ts/.js files load. “A plugins/ directory beside a project-root opencode.json(c) is not discovered automatically.” O plugins
CONFIRMED (V2 docs, build/plugins/server): tool hook await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", (event) => { if (event.tool === "read") console.log(event.input) }); “the hook receives the call and can inspect or change its input”. V1 key was "tool.execute.before". After: ctx.tool.hook("execute.after", ...). O build/plugins/server
CONFIRMED: permission hook ctx.permission.hook("evaluate", ...); “Hooks run for allow and ask decisions.”; “An explicit configured deny is final and does not invoke the hook.”; “A hook may change effect to allow, ask, or deny.”; event.message is the denial reason. O build/plugins/server
CONFIRMED: “The docs don’t describe throwing from a tool hook to block a call” (summariser’s statement); documented deny route is the permission evaluate hook. UNCONFIRMED: whether throwing in execute.before blocks (V1 community pattern, not in fetched docs).
UNCONFIRMED: a trust/security statement for plugins (none found). Treat plugins as code running with your privileges (inference, same as Claude hooks).
CONFIRMED: two built-in policy plugins “ignore removals so that a repository cannot switch off” policy. O plugins
UNCONFIRMED: a direct exit-code-2 equivalent; OpenCode has no shell-hook config documented in pages read.

title: Skills portability and team skills: GitHub Blog article
text:
Read 2026-11-17. Source: https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/build-once-run-on-any-agent-a-practical-guide-to-agent-skills/ (“Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills”, Andrea Griffiths, GitHub Blog, 2026-11-12). Method: page fetched through a summarising fetch tool, so everything below is a paraphrase of a summary, not a quote. Re-read the article before quoting. Reuse: footer “© 2026 GitHub, Inc.”; no licence for the article text is stated; github.blog/robots.txt has no AI-crawler rules and no Content-Signal line. Copyright is therefore reserved: use the ideas in our own words with credit and a link; copy no text. Decision fed: advice added to the Forge a Skill, Test the Skill and Bundle a Plugin quests, plus Lore links.



CONFIRMED (article): a skill is a versioned folder built around a SKILL.md that says when and how to do a repeatable task. Its value is that team knowledge stops living in chats or in one person’s head.
CONFIRMED: a skill describes the method; the environment that runs it still supplies the tools, credentials and permissions. A skill is not an access grant.
CONFIRMED: skills fit bounded, repeatable work (checklists, releases, migrations, metric pipelines). Work that needs stable interfaces, shared state, audit trails, long-running control or externally enforced permissions is better built as an application.
CONFIRMED: one skill, one clear job, with a defined input and output. Frontmatter name and description should say the task and purpose. Include a “when to use” section, what to review, and what evidence to report back.
CONFIRMED: start with a task you find yourself explaining repeatedly; define its inputs, its boundaries and what a reviewer needs to see.
CONFIRMED: use a separate verifier for AI-generated work. An agent judging its own output is not an independent check. (The demo’s verifier returns PASS, FAIL or PARTIAL and must cite evidence from the changed files.)
CONFIRMED: portability: write the instructions once and reuse across agent clients, but clients differ in models, tools, credentials and permissions, so verify in each client. After installing, check the client triggers the skill for the right task, loads its references, uses the tools it needs and returns the expected evidence.
CONFIRMED: the worked example keeps skills/*/SKILL.md as the single source, generates client-specific packaging (it names Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot), and runs a check mode in CI to catch drift between source and generated copies.
CONFIRMED: split a larger workflow into skills with distinct responsibilities that share project context instead of each rediscovering it; changing one step should touch one skill. Keep project names, databases and conventions in one manifest the skills read instead of hardcoding them; keep discovered details separate from team standards (a pattern found in code is not automatically a rule); have people confirm discovered details where judgment matters. Portability test: could another team reuse the skills with its own manifest without rewriting them?
CONFIRMED: the example workflow has human checkpoints in each phase and requires approval before schema changes run. Blocking a merge depends on repository rules and required CI checks, not on the skill alone. The demo’s review action reads diffs statically and was advisory.
CONFIRMED (the article’s own three-line summary, paraphrased): put business context in one manifest; use one consistent access path across related skills; use instructions to guide, and tests, CI checks and human review to verify.





An ‘open standard’ discussion, a detailed testing method, a folder layout beyond SKILL.md, a dedicated security section. (Security appears only implicitly: permissions stay with the host.) Do not credit the article for the Agent Skills standard or for eval design; those come from the Anthropic and OpenCode docs already in research/forge.md and research/terminology.md.
UNCONFIRMED: the demo repositories’ licence.





Add an agent skill to GitHub Copilot (GitHub docs): https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/customize-copilot/customize-cloud-agent/add-skills (not read by us)
Demo repository: https://github.com/githubevents/build-once-run-on-any-agent (demos: proof-agent, dataforge; not read by us)

CONFIRMED: start with a task you find yourself explaining repeatedly; define its inputs, its boundaries and what a reviewer needs to see.
CONFIRMED: use a separate verifier for AI-generated work. An agent judging its own output is not an independent check. (The demo’s verifier returns PASS, FAIL or PARTIAL and must cite evidence from the changed files.)
CONFIRMED: portability: write the instructions once and reuse across agent clients, but clients differ in models, tools, credentials and permissions, so verify in each client. After installing, check the client triggers the skill for the right task, loads its references, uses the tools it needs and returns the expected evidence.
CONFIRMED: the worked example keeps skills/*/SKILL.md as the single source, generates client-specific packaging (it names Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot), and runs a check mode in CI to catch drift between source and generated copies.
CONFIRMED: split a larger workflow into skills with distinct responsibilities that share project context instead of each rediscovering it; changing one step should touch one skill. Keep project names, databases and conventions in one manifest the skills read instead of hardcoding them; keep discovered details separate from team standards (a pattern found in code is not automatically a rule); have people confirm discovered details where judgment matters. Portability test: could another team reuse the skills with its own manifest without rewriting them?
CONFIRMED: the example workflow has human checkpoints in each phase and requires approval before schema changes run. Blocking a merge depends on repository rules and required CI checks, not on the skill alone. The demo’s review action reads diffs statically and was advisory.
CONFIRMED (the article’s own three-line summary, paraphrased): put business context in one manifest; use one consistent access path across related skills; use instructions to guide, and tests, CI checks and human review to verify.

title: Privacy and unpublished work
text:
Date checked 2026-11-17. Official docs only, via a summarising fetch tool (quotes as returned). Question: what do the docs say about retention and training use, so the Crypt quest can advise on unpublished ideas and results. Feeds: zones/crypt/secrets-and-sensitive-ground.qmd; zones/reef/send-small-say-so.qmd (disclosure section).



CONFIRMED training, consumer (Free, Pro, Max, Ultra): “We give you the choice to allow your data to be used to improve future Claude models.” Anthropic trains new models on data from these accounts “when this setting is on (including when you use Claude Code from these accounts)”.
CONFIRMED training, commercial (Team, Enterprise, API, 3rd-party platforms, Claude Gov): “Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms, unless the customer has chosen to provide their data to us for model improvement (for example, the Developer Partner Program).”
CONFIRMED retention, consumer: 5 years if data use for model improvement is allowed; 30 days if not. Setting at https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls.
CONFIRMED retention, commercial (Team, Enterprise, API): standard 30 days; zero data retention available to qualified Enterprise accounts, enabled per organisation.
CONFIRMED: Claude Code sends all user prompts and model outputs over the network (TLS 1.2+); local transcripts are stored in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).
CONFIRMED: transcripts sent with /feedback are retained for 5 years.
Scope: this page covers Claude Code. Not checked: the claude.ai chat product’s privacy help pages, Anthropic’s Privacy Center and the Consumer and Commercial Terms text themselves (linked from the page). Not checked: how any other vendor’s consumer chat tool handles training or retention.





CONFIRMED: “Ollama runs locally. We don’t see your prompts or data when you run locally.”
CONFIRMED: cloud models are different: Ollama processes prompts and responses to deliver the service; the FAQ says they are not stored or logged and never used for training. Local-only mode: OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or disable_ollama_cloud in ~/.ollama/server.json.
Not checked: Ollama’s separate Cloud FAQ, and whether tools or web search used alongside a local model send data elsewhere.





Not checked: any journal or funder policy on disclosing AI assistance. No venue was read, so the quest names none and tells readers to check the venue’s own page.
General practice: preprints, repository tags and lab notebook entries date-stamp work. Not checked against a primary source here.

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text:
Live spot-check, 2026-11-17 (later the same day, via summarising fetch): model-config (aliases, set order, pinning variables, effort levels, defaults), effort (platform), sub-agents (frontmatter, resolution order, Explore/Plan skip CLAUDE.md, Explore model), costs (/usage), choosing-a-model and optimizing-for-cost (cheap-then-retry, cost per completed task) were re-read; the first fetch of model-config and sub-agents each covered only the first 100k characters, and optimizing-for-cost the first 100k of about 216k, so later sections remain unread. Everything below was otherwise first-pass. Finding: Claude Code model-config says the default effort for Sonnet 5.5 (and Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2) is medium; the API effort page and choosing-a-model say Sonnet 5.5 is high on the API. So the pages differ by surface (Claude Code vs API) rather than contradicting each other; the quest names the surface. The Nov 9 claude.dev article’s table says the same (high on the API, medium in Claude Code).
Checked 2026-11-17. Official docs only, plus one flagged secondary article. Pages came through a summarising fetch tool (quotes as returned; paraphrase on the site). Docs pages show no publish date; model-config, sub-agents, skills and choosing-a-model pages were read only in their first ~100k characters. Base: P = https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/ ; C = https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ ; O = https://opencode.ai/docs/ Not repeated: effort levels list, API effort wording, Claude Code effort defaults, max overthinking quotes, ultrathink (research/terminology.md section 6); /context, /clear, subagent context isolation, /usage cost basics (session-management.md, fundamentals.md). Decision fed: quest text on picking a model, tuning effort, delegating reading to cheaper subagents.



CONFIRMED: four tiers in the selection matrix. Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2): highest capability, hours-long agent sessions and deep research. Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5): complex agentic coding. Sonnet 5.5: “speed and capability for everyday coding, agent, and enterprise workloads”. Haiku 5.5: lowest latency and price, lists “subagent tasks”.
CONFIRMED: “Most workloads start with Claude Opus 5.5.” Fable 5.2 is “most capable model open to all customers”; Mythos 5.2 has the same capabilities for verified organisations only.
CONFIRMED relative cost: Opus 5.5 costs half as much per token as Fable 5.2 (stated in the article only; P fast-mode shows fast prices of $8/$40 per MTok Opus 5.5 vs $16/$80 Fable 5.2, which is the fast-mode rate, not standard). Standard prices live in the models overview table (not fetched). Do not print per-token prices on the site.
UNCONFIRMED: Haiku 5.5 price rising above 100K-token prompts (article claim only).
CONFIRMED: two start strategies: efficiency-first (Haiku, upgrade if needed) or capability-first (Opus 5.5, then lower effort or downgrade). Move to Fable 5.2 if evals at xhigh/max still fall short.
CONFIRMED: fast mode = same model, “up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second” at premium pricing, on Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, Opus 5.5 (Opus 5 research preview; Opus 4.8 deprecated, removal 2026-11-30). API field speed: "fast"; not with Batch API or Priority Tier; falling back to standard misses the prompt cache. P build-with-claude/fast-mode
UNCONFIRMED: how fast mode is switched on in Claude Code (costs page links to C fast-mode, not fetched). Leave it out of quests.





CONFIRMED aliases, exactly: default (clears an override; “not itself a model alias”), best (same as opus), fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m], opus[1m], opusplan (opus in plan mode, then sonnet for execution).
CONFIRMED: on the Anthropic API opus = Opus 5.5, sonnet = Sonnet 5.5, haiku = Haiku 5.5. Other providers resolve aliases to earlier versions (example: Foundry gives Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.5).
CONFIRMED set-model order of priority: /model <alias|name> in session (alone opens picker; Enter saves as default, s for this session only); claude --model <alias|name>; env ANTHROPIC_MODEL; settings field model; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL for new sessions (v2.1.236+).
CONFIRMED pinning: use a full name such as claude-opus-5-5, or set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL.
CONFIRMED default model: Opus 5.5 on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise and API; Sonnet 4.5 on Foundry; an admin default overrides. Admins restrict with availableModels (+ enforceAvailableModels).
CONFIRMED: switching models “can change how prompt caching behaves”; Claude Code may ask you to confirm. /model switches also reach subagents that inherit.
Reproducibility (inference): aliases move when a new version ships, so a lab pipeline or course material that must give the same results pins a full name.





CONFIRMED set methods: /effort, --effort, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, settings effortLevel, per-model modelSettings; CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=auto sends no level. ultracode is a Claude Code setting for dynamic workflows, “not a model effort level”. C model-config
CONFIRMED skill frontmatter model: same values as /model, or inherit; applies for the rest of the turn only, not saved; ignored if availableModels excludes it. effort: low|medium|high|xhigh|max (levels depend on the model); turn-only; overrides session effort but not CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. With context: fork both apply to the forked subagent instead. Example in the docs: model: opus, effort: high. C skills
CONFIRMED API defaults (differs from the Claude Code list in terminology.md): high everywhere except medium on Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, so Sonnet 5.5 is high on the API page. P effort. The Claude Code default for Sonnet 5.5 is medium per terminology.md; the two pages disagree, so name the surface.
CONFIRMED model-specific advice: Opus 5.5 default medium; Sonnet 5.5: medium for well-specified agentic coding, high for harder or longer, xhigh/max only where evals show a gain; Haiku 5.5: start medium, and at low it “is more likely to skip a search, stop early, or skip a check”. P effort
CONFIRMED: low listed for “simpler tasks… such as subagents”. Lower effort means fewer, terser tool calls. P effort
CONFIRMED: “Tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models.” P choosing-a-model
CONFIRMED cost data (Anthropic-internal, “directional”): Sonnet 5.5 medium scored about 7 points below high for about 59% of the cost on long-horizon coding. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: sweep effort in separate sessions; changing effort mid-session invalidates the cache (top-level effort; per-message effort on supported models keeps it). P optimizing-for-cost, effort
CONFIRMED: at xhigh/max Sonnet 5.5 may start extra review rounds; a scoping prompt keeps it on task. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: Opus 4.7 at low/medium scopes work to what was asked; if reasoning looks shallow on hard problems, raise effort rather than prompt around it. P effort
CONFIRMED (cost-saving pattern): if outcomes are checkable (tests, a verifier), run at low, re-run only failures at high. Anthropic measure: Opus 5.5 about 97% solved at ~$0.17/task vs 95.3% at $0.29 all-high (SWE-bench Pro subset). Caveats: a checker that passes bad work lets failures through; failures take two runs of wall time. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: compare “cost per completed task, not cost per token”; “price the tail” (two of 20 problems carried 43% of spend); failed tasks still bill. P optimizing-for-cost





CONFIRMED subagent model accepts sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full ID (e.g. claude-opus-5-5), or inherit. Omitted = resolution order, not literally inherit. effort accepts low|medium|high|xhigh|max; it overrides session effort but not CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. If the subagent’s model differs from the main one and has no effort, the session level does not apply, so set it.
CONFIRMED resolution order (first wins): per-invocation model parameter; definition model; env CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL; the main conversation’s model. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL alone does not change built-in Explore/Plan. Forcing: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257+) ignores definition and per-call models.
CONFIRMED built-ins: general-purpose and Plan follow the parent model; statusline-setup Sonnet; claude-code-guide Haiku. Explore: page says “the parent conversation’s model”, then (as returned) that with a subscription/Console/gateway it runs on the Opus the alias resolves to. A user subagent named Explore overrides it (example model: haiku). The Explore wording is contradictory in the summary; re-read before quoting.
CONFIRMED context/cost benefits: exploration stays out of the main conversation; only a summary returns; “control costs by routing tasks to faster, lower-cost models like Haiku”. Caveats: subagent requests count toward the same usage limits; many subagents returning detailed results “can consume significant context”.
CONFIRMED CLAUDE.md: non-fork subagents load the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, except built-in Explore and Plan (skipped for speed); omitClaudeMd: true skips it in a custom one. Subagents do not inherit output style or auto memory. Restate must-have rules in the delegation prompt.
CONFIRMED: subagents inherit the session thinking setting (no per-subagent setting); nested subagents inherit their spawner’s model; /tasks shows each running subagent’s model and effort (v2.1.242+).
CONFIRMED: orchestrator pattern helped only for routine work with a long cost tail or work larger than one context; for one dependent chain that fits in one context, single model at lower effort won. Opus 5.5 over Sonnet 5.5 subagents cost about a third less on defect search with similar score; Haiku 5.5 subagents on coding “were not better than simply lowering effort”. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: build a multimodel setup only if it beats the single model’s whole score-vs-spend curve. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: Agent teams: “Use Sonnet for teammates”; about 7x tokens of a standard session in plan mode (C costs).





CONFIRMED /usage: Session block shows total cost, API and wall duration, lines changed, and “Usage by model” (input, output, cache read/write tokens, $ per model). Dollar figure is computed locally at list price (or admin modelPricing), an estimate. Resets on /clear (v2.1.211+). Subscribers see plan usage bars instead of meaningful $.
CONFIRMED: /usage Session block also has a Prompt cache (main) line (v2.1.251+; main conversation only, not subagents). Plan breakdown attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, with recommendations (f applies, v2.1.305+).
CONFIRMED: /insights writes an HTML report of how you work. Status line can show cost/context.
NOT FOUND in these pages: a /cost command. Do not teach /cost; use /usage.
CONFIRMED: Anthropic average about $13 per developer per active day (enterprise deployments); 90% below $30.





CONFIRMED: /models picks for this session only (config unchanged); opencode run --model provider/model-id; model key in opencode.json/opencode.jsonc sets the default, falling back to the newest available model if unavailable. Format provider/model-id, optional #variant (e.g. ...#high); IDs case-sensitive.
CONFIRMED per-agent: model key on an agent (markdown frontmatter string, or JSONC object with providerID, model, variant). Frontmatter example: mode: subagent, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5#high. A subagent without model inherits the parent session model. Built-ins: build, plan (primary), general, explore (subagents). The page does not say which model each built-in uses.
UNCONFIRMED: a small_model key (not on the page). Note the JSONC example uses top-level key agents; verify against the schema before copying.
CONFIRMED local models: Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434 is auto-discovered under provider ollama (e.g. ollama/gemma3:4b); change host with providers.ollama.settings.baseURL; LM Studio and vLLM likewise; disable discovery with "plugins": ["-opencode.provider.ollama"].
UNCONFIRMED: that a local model is good enough as a cheap delegate, its cost, or tool-use quality. The docs only say it can be selected.





UNCONFIRMED: any Claude doc page on running Ollama as a Claude Code subagent. Claude Code subagent model values are Claude aliases or Claude IDs only (section 4). Ollama is an OpenCode-only claim on these pages. (Gateway use via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL appears on the sub-agents page but was not pursued.)





CONFIRMED: on the API, a thinking block is tied to the preceding prompt, the model and the account. A model that cannot read another’s blocks drops them for that request, no error, no billing; switching back reads them again. Haiku 5.5 to Opus 5.5 keeps reasoning; Opus 5.5 to Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 does not; Fable 5.2 to anything else drops it. Useful only as “switching down loses earlier reasoning”; Claude Code handles this itself.
CONFIRMED: per-turn model overrides in skills last one turn; /model switch persists.




This is a different article from the cloud field guide dated 2026-10-06 in research/claude-cloud.md; the two dates belong to two articles. The blog index lists no byline for this post, the article page does. The page does not say who runs the site. Provenance not confirmed, no reuse licence, benchmark numbers vendor-run and unverified. Ideas paraphrased only; cite as “one article” or not at all. Mapped to the official docs: - Default Opus 5.5 at medium; step down to Sonnet 5.5 for well-scoped fixes; Haiku for classification and extraction and as subagent; Fable 5.2 for hardest work. Official docs support this tiering (P choosing-a-model, optimizing). The per-task-type table is ARTICLE-ONLY in detail (bug fixes vs migrations). - Raise effort before switching models. Official: partly (P choosing-a-model “better lever”). “Past high one more level can cost as much as a larger model; test the next model up at lower effort” is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Effort cannot add knowledge the model lacks: ARTICLE-ONLY (the docs say higher effort adds thoroughness, not this). - Order: give a check first, then raise effort, then change model: ARTICLE-ONLY as a sequence; the docs do say to give verification targets (C costs). - Run checkable tasks at low, re-run failures at high: official (section 3). - Cost per finished task, not per token; price the hardest tasks: official. - Keep expensive-model context lean, push bulk reading to cheaper subagents; edits stay on the main model: official for delegation benefits; “keep edits on the main model” is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Switching models mid-conversation misses the cache; compact or start fresh first: partly official (model-config note, preserved-thinking). The specific “compact first” tip is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Pin a subagent’s model in its definition (article example model: haiku, tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, “log-reader”), and define your own Explore on Haiku: official (section 4). - opusplan caution (puts edits on the smaller model; measure on own tasks): the alias is official; the caution is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Test on your own tasks with outcome checks, separate sessions per effort level: official (P optimizing-for-cost, choosing-a-model).




Documented: aliases above; /model, --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL, settings model; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU,FABLE}_MODEL; /effort, --effort, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, effortLevel, modelSettings; frontmatter model, effort (skills and subagents), omitClaudeMd; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE; availableModels; /usage, /insights, /tasks; MAX_THINKING_TOKENS (fixed-budget models only; adaptive models ignore it); API output_config.effort, speed: "fast".
NOT documented in these pages: /cost, --subagent-model, a per-subagent thinking setting, small_model, any Ollama-via-Claude-Code route, a documented price table in these pages.





Read C model-config past 100k (effort resolution order, auto-compact window) and C fast-mode before quoting.
Re-read Explore wording on C sub-agents.

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text:
CONFIRMED subagent model accepts sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full ID (e.g. claude-opus-5-5), or inherit. Omitted = resolution order, not literally inherit. effort accepts low|medium|high|xhigh|max; it overrides session effort but not CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. If the subagent’s model differs from the main one and has no effort, the session level does not apply, so set it.
CONFIRMED resolution order (first wins): per-invocation model parameter; definition model; env CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL; the main conversation’s model. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL alone does not change built-in Explore/Plan. Forcing: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257+) ignores definition and per-call models.
CONFIRMED built-ins: general-purpose and Plan follow the parent model; statusline-setup Sonnet; claude-code-guide Haiku. Explore: page says “the parent conversation’s model”, then (as returned) that with a subscription/Console/gateway it runs on the Opus the alias resolves to. A user subagent named Explore overrides it (example model: haiku). The Explore wording is contradictory in the summary; re-read before quoting.
CONFIRMED context/cost benefits: exploration stays out of the main conversation; only a summary returns; “control costs by routing tasks to faster, lower-cost models like Haiku”. Caveats: subagent requests count toward the same usage limits; many subagents returning detailed results “can consume significant context”.
CONFIRMED CLAUDE.md: non-fork subagents load the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, except built-in Explore and Plan (skipped for speed); omitClaudeMd: true skips it in a custom one. Subagents do not inherit output style or auto memory. Restate must-have rules in the delegation prompt.
CONFIRMED: subagents inherit the session thinking setting (no per-subagent setting); nested subagents inherit their spawner’s model; /tasks shows each running subagent’s model and effort (v2.1.242+).
CONFIRMED: orchestrator pattern helped only for routine work with a long cost tail or work larger than one context; for one dependent chain that fits in one context, single model at lower effort won. Opus 5.5 over Sonnet 5.5 subagents cost about a third less on defect search with similar score; Haiku 5.5 subagents on coding “were not better than simply lowering effort”. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: build a multimodel setup only if it beats the single model’s whole score-vs-spend curve. P optimizing-for-cost
CONFIRMED: Agent teams: “Use Sonnet for teammates”; about 7x tokens of a standard session in plan mode (C costs).

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text:
CONFIRMED /usage: Session block shows total cost, API and wall duration, lines changed, and “Usage by model” (input, output, cache read/write tokens, $ per model). Dollar figure is computed locally at list price (or admin modelPricing), an estimate. Resets on /clear (v2.1.211+). Subscribers see plan usage bars instead of meaningful $.
CONFIRMED: /usage Session block also has a Prompt cache (main) line (v2.1.251+; main conversation only, not subagents). Plan breakdown attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, with recommendations (f applies, v2.1.305+).
CONFIRMED: /insights writes an HTML report of how you work. Status line can show cost/context.
NOT FOUND in these pages: a /cost command. Do not teach /cost; use /usage.
CONFIRMED: Anthropic average about $13 per developer per active day (enterprise deployments); 90% below $30.

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text:
CONFIRMED: /models picks for this session only (config unchanged); opencode run --model provider/model-id; model key in opencode.json/opencode.jsonc sets the default, falling back to the newest available model if unavailable. Format provider/model-id, optional #variant (e.g. ...#high); IDs case-sensitive.
CONFIRMED per-agent: model key on an agent (markdown frontmatter string, or JSONC object with providerID, model, variant). Frontmatter example: mode: subagent, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5#high. A subagent without model inherits the parent session model. Built-ins: build, plan (primary), general, explore (subagents). The page does not say which model each built-in uses.
UNCONFIRMED: a small_model key (not on the page). Note the JSONC example uses top-level key agents; verify against the schema before copying.
CONFIRMED local models: Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434 is auto-discovered under provider ollama (e.g. ollama/gemma3:4b); change host with providers.ollama.settings.baseURL; LM Studio and vLLM likewise; disable discovery with "plugins": ["-opencode.provider.ollama"].
UNCONFIRMED: that a local model is good enough as a cheap delegate, its cost, or tool-use quality. The docs only say it can be selected.

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text: UNCONFIRMED: any Claude doc page on running Ollama as a Claude Code subagent. Claude Code subagent model values are Claude aliases or Claude IDs only (section 4). Ollama is an OpenCode-only claim on these pages. (Gateway use via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL appears on the sub-agents page but was not pursued.)

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text:
CONFIRMED: on the API, a thinking block is tied to the preceding prompt, the model and the account. A model that cannot read another’s blocks drops them for that request, no error, no billing; switching back reads them again. Haiku 5.5 to Opus 5.5 keeps reasoning; Opus 5.5 to Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 does not; Fable 5.2 to anything else drops it. Useful only as “switching down loses earlier reasoning”; Claude Code handles this itself.
CONFIRMED: per-turn model overrides in skills last one turn; /model switch persists.

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text: This is a different article from the cloud field guide dated 2026-10-06 in research/claude-cloud.md; the two dates belong to two articles. The blog index lists no byline for this post, the article page does. The page does not say who runs the site. Provenance not confirmed, no reuse licence, benchmark numbers vendor-run and unverified. Ideas paraphrased only; cite as “one article” or not at all. Mapped to the official docs: - Default Opus 5.5 at medium; step down to Sonnet 5.5 for well-scoped fixes; Haiku for classification and extraction and as subagent; Fable 5.2 for hardest work. Official docs support this tiering (P choosing-a-model, optimizing). The per-task-type table is ARTICLE-ONLY in detail (bug fixes vs migrations). - Raise effort before switching models. Official: partly (P choosing-a-model “better lever”). “Past high one more level can cost as much as a larger model; test the next model up at lower effort” is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Effort cannot add knowledge the model lacks: ARTICLE-ONLY (the docs say higher effort adds thoroughness, not this). - Order: give a check first, then raise effort, then change model: ARTICLE-ONLY as a sequence; the docs do say to give verification targets (C costs). - Run checkable tasks at low, re-run failures at high: official (section 3). - Cost per finished task, not per token; price the hardest tasks: official. - Keep expensive-model context lean, push bulk reading to cheaper subagents; edits stay on the main model: official for delegation benefits; “keep edits on the main model” is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Switching models mid-conversation misses the cache; compact or start fresh first: partly official (model-config note, preserved-thinking). The specific “compact first” tip is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Pin a subagent’s model in its definition (article example model: haiku, tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, “log-reader”), and define your own Explore on Haiku: official (section 4). - opusplan caution (puts edits on the smaller model; measure on own tasks): the alias is official; the caution is ARTICLE-ONLY. - Test on your own tasks with outcome checks, separate sessions per effort level: official (P optimizing-for-cost, choosing-a-model).

title: Model choice, effort and delegation
text:
Documented: aliases above; /model, --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL, settings model; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU,FABLE}_MODEL; /effort, --effort, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, effortLevel, modelSettings; frontmatter model, effort (skills and subagents), omitClaudeMd; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE; availableModels; /usage, /insights, /tasks; MAX_THINKING_TOKENS (fixed-budget models only; adaptive models ignore it); API output_config.effort, speed: "fast".
NOT documented in these pages: /cost, --subagent-model, a per-subagent thinking setting, small_model, any Ollama-via-Claude-Code route, a documented price table in these pages.
