title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED: a Claude Code session on cloud infrastructure instead of your machine; Anthropic-managed by default, or an org self-hosted environment when routed there. Keeps running after you close the laptop. C CW
CONFIRMED: each session = fresh Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 VM with your repo cloned; clone happens fresh every session. C CE, C WQ
CONFIRMED: local sessions run on your machine and use local config; cloud uses “repo only”. C WQ (comparison table)
CONFIRMED what travels: everything committed (CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules, skills, agents, commands; hooks/permissions/.mcp.json in a one-repo session). C CE “What carries over”
CONFIRMED what does NOT travel: user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/skills|agents|commands, user-scoped plugins and settings, claude mcp add servers at local/user scope, ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, plugins declared in repo settings, interactive auth such as AWS SSO, MDM/managed-settings files on your device. Org server-managed settings DO apply. C CE, C SET “Settings in cloud sessions”
CONFIRMED: personal preferences can be written by a setup script to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md in the VM. C CE
CONFIRMED: Remote Control is different: code runs on YOUR machine, only the transcript syncs through Anthropic. C SEC, C DU

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED: browser https://claude.ai/code (“Claude Code on the web”); mobile: Code tab in the Claude app; Desktop: choose Cloud in the environment selector; terminal claude --cloud "task"; scheduled tasks (routines) also run as cloud sessions. C CW
CONFIRMED: --cloud clones the GitHub remote at your current branch, not your local checkout; push first. One repo at a time. --remote is a deprecated alias. C CW
CONFIRMED: if the branch is not on GitHub the CLI prints Branch <name> is not on GitHub and the session starts from a pushed commit or default branch; unpushed commits and uncommitted changes are absent. C CW
CONFIRMED: no GitHub remote or no Claude GitHub App on the repo: Claude Code bundles and uploads the local repo (full history all branches plus uncommitted changes to tracked files; <100 MB; untracked files excluded; on macOS/Linux/WSL needs git 2.31+ and a supported checkout layout, else the CLI prints Not uploading this working tree: and does not start the session; native Windows skips those checks; re-confirmed live 2026-11-17). On macOS/Linux/WSL uncommitted changes to .env, *.tfvars, id_rsa, *.pem and git-filter-managed (LFS) files are left out; on native Windows everything tracked uploads as is. CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1 forces a bundle. C CW
CONFIRMED: claude --teleport (picker) / claude --teleport <session-id>; in-session /teleport or /tp; /tasks then t; claude.ai/code Open in > Terminal. C CW
CONFIRMED teleport needs: clean git state (it offers to stash), same repo (not a fork), branch pushed, same claude.ai account. Handoff is one-way from CLI (cloud to terminal); Desktop can send a local session to cloud via Open in > Cloud (conversation carried as a summary). C CW, C DESK
CONFIRMED: follow-up from any machine: claude -p "message" --cloud <session-id>. C CW
CONFIRMED: /web-setup (inside the CLI, not the shell) sends your gh auth token to Anthropic; /login with claude.ai needed; API-key or Console sign-in does not work. --cloud/--teleport unavailable with Bedrock/Vertex-style providers. C WQ, C CW
CONFIRMED: prefill URL params prompt (alias q), prompt_url, repositories (alias repo), environment. C WQ
CONFIRMED: /autofix-pr, Auto-fix toggle, /mobile (QR to app store), /schedule. C CW, C WQ, C MOB
NOT documented here: a claude cloud subcommand; any flag to choose permission mode for --cloud (mode is picked in the UI dropdown).

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED two methods. (a) Claude GitHub App via web onboarding: any public repo, plus private repos the App is installed on. (b) /web-setup: any repo your gh token can reach, App not needed. C CW
CONFIRMED: Auto-fix and Projects need the App installed on the repo. Org owners may need to approve installs. C CW, C WQ
CONFIRMED: Team/Enterprise: an Owner must enable the GitHub connector (Organization settings > Connectors); /web-setup hidden until Owner enables Quick setup (Organization settings > Claude Code). C WQ, C CW
CONFIRMED credential handling (Anthropic-hosted): GitHub credentials stored encrypted on Anthropic servers, never enter the VM; VM holds a short-lived credential scoped to the session; a GitHub proxy swaps it. C CW, C SEC, C DU
CONFIRMED proxy limits: rejects branch deletion and non-branch pushes (tags); does NOT limit which branches a push can update, so use GitHub branch protection or rulesets (a rule the connected access can bypass will not block the push). API requests only for repos attached to the session (403 otherwise); GraphQL blocked (so gh pr/gh issue fail; REST via gh api works). C CE “GitHub proxy”, C SEC
UNCONFIRMED: a documented per-branch credential. The docs describe session-scoped credentials, not branch-scoped ones. Do not teach “branch-limited token”.
CONFIRMED: /web-setup token lives encrypted with your account until removed at claude.ai/customize/connectors (that does not revoke it on GitHub). Token may warn about missing workflow scope. C WQ
CONFIRMED: non-GitHub hosts: only as local bundle, cannot push back; PR creation needs GitHub; GitHub Enterprise Server supported on Team/Enterprise. C CW

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED: an environment = saved config (network access, env vars, setup script, network secrets). Onboarding creates Default with Limited access, no vars, no script. Edited via the selector at claude.ai/code (“New environment”, “Network access”, “Setup script”, “Environment variables”). C CE
CONFIRMED network access levels (current names): None, Limited (default allowlist of package registries, GitHub, cloud SDKs while “Allow package managers” is checked, plus your “Allowed domains”, *. wildcard), Full. Old names Trusted and Custom map to Limited. (Blog names None/Trusted/Custom/Full: ARTICLE-ONLY, outdated vs docs.) C CE
CONFIRMED: at every level these still work: GitHub via proxy, enabled MCP connectors (traffic via Anthropic servers), hosts of network secrets, and the Anthropic API even at None. No org-level allowlist can be pushed; use an org-shared environment. C CE, C CW
CONFIRMED env vars: .env format; any command Claude runs can read them; “Anyone who uses the environment can read the values”; docs say use network secrets instead where possible. Vars read at session create and when VM restored. C CE
CONFIRMED network secrets: key stays outside VM; Anthropic’s agent proxy adds it to requests for hosts you list. Not for GitHub, api.anthropic.com or public registries (pypi, npm, crates, go proxy), setup-script requests, telemetry. Unavailable with self-hosted envs or customer-managed encryption keys. C CE
CONFIRMED setup script: Bash, runs as root before Claude launches, must exit 0, keep under ~5 minutes (else not cached), env vars not yet set when it runs, installs need network (None blocks them). Up to 64 KB. C CE
CONFIRMED caching: filesystem snapshot after setup; packages, images and files persist; running processes/DBs do not. Rebuilt when script or allowed hosts change or after ~7 days. Not re-run when an idle VM is restored. C CE
CONFIRMED preinstalled: Python (pip, uv, poetry, pytest), Node 20/21/22, Ruby, PHP, Java 21, Go, Rust, C/C++, Docker, PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, Chrome for Testing, git, gh, jq. No R, conda or bioinformatics tools are listed; .NET not installed. Ask Claude to run check-tools. C CE
CONFIRMED: SessionStart hooks (from committed settings) run on every session; setup scripts are cloud-only. C CE

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED code storage: repo is cloned into the session VM; “Anthropic stores the session transcript so you can return to the session later”; code and session data follow the retention and usage policies for your account type. C DU
CONFIRMED all outbound traffic from Anthropic-hosted sessions goes through a security proxy for audit logging and abuse prevention. C DU, C CE
CONFIRMED training: consumer plans (Free/Pro/Max/Ultra): training only if the setting is on, including Claude Code; commercial (Team, Enterprise, API): not trained on code or prompts unless the customer opts in (e.g. Development Partner Program). C DU
CONFIRMED retention: consumer 5 years if training allowed, 30 days if not; commercial standard 30 days; ZDR for qualified Enterprise accounts. Deleting a cloud session permanently removes its event data. C DU, C CW
CONFIRMED: ZDR not included in standard Enterprise; per-organization enablement by Anthropic. C ZDR
CONFIRMED: with ZDR, cloud sessions (including from Desktop) are disabled at the backend because they need server-side storage of prompts/completions. Same for Remote Control, Claude Tag, /feedback. C ZDR
CONFIRMED: organizations with HIPAA configuration, or ZDR, cannot use cloud sessions or /web-setup; customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) orgs cannot start cloud sessions. HIPAA coverage is for local mode (CLI, Desktop Code tab). C CW, C WQ, C ZDR
CONFIRMED security model (Anthropic-hosted): isolated VM per session; network limited by default; credentials outside the sandbox; audit logging; VMs reclaimed after inactivity. C SEC, C CW
CONFIRMED caveat: with network access None, Claude Code still talks to the Anthropic API, “which may allow data to exit the VM”. C CW
CONFIRMED sharing: Team/Enterprise visibility Private or Team; Pro/Max/Ultra Private or Public (any claude.ai user), repo verification off by default. Docs warn sessions may contain code and credentials from private repos. C CW
CONFIRMED: Anthropic reads only the repo you start the session in, not other connected repos. C DU
CONFIRMED: Claude can reply on PRs under your GitHub name (labelled as Claude Code), which can trigger comment-driven automation (Atlantis, Terraform Cloud, issue_comment workflows). C CW
NOT documented: any guidance specific to genomic, patient, human-subject or controlled-access data (dbGaP, EGA, GDPR) for cloud sessions; no data-residency statement found for cloud sessions. UNCONFIRMED. Teaching inference (ours, not a doc claim): treat the clone, transcript and any pasted data as stored by Anthropic; keep controlled data out of the repo, and ask your data-access committee before any cloud use.

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED: available on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team; Enterprise only with premium seats or Chat + Claude Code seats; custom roles need a “cloud sessions” permission. C CW
CONFIRMED: usage counts toward plan limits shared with all other Claude and Claude Code use; no separate VM charge; parallel tasks use limits proportionately. C CW, C WQ
CONFIRMED: org policy allow_remote_sessions must be on (Owner: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code). C CW
UNCONFIRMED: a beta or research-preview label. None appeared on the CW/WQ pages as fetched. Re-check before publishing.

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED VM ceilings (approximate, may change): 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, 30 GB disk; heavy jobs may be stopped. Docs point to Remote Control (your hardware) or a self-hosted environment. C CE
CONFIRMED timeouts: foreground command 2 min default, up to 10; then moved to background up to 30 more minutes; SessionStart hook 600 s; env vars BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS. C CE
CONFIRMED idle: VM pauses after a few minutes with files saved, may later be reclaimed. Reopening restores conversation history only; running shell commands, subagents, session-scoped schedules and /loop are lost. Waiting on an MCP approval counts as idle. C CW, C CE
CONFIRMED: x86_64 only; use x86_64 Linux builds. Interactive SSO unsupported. Docs do not list GPUs.
NOT documented: GPU, VPN or on-prem network access, mounting local or HPC filesystems, large data upload. UNCONFIRMED; inference from the above: no local DBs/VPN/HPC and 30 GB disk. Mark as inference.
CONFIRMED: Anthropic-hosted needs GitHub for clone/PR; claude --cloud fails on API-key/third-party-provider auth. C CW

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
CONFIRMED: cloud offers Accept edits (corresponds to default), Plan, Auto (unless org disables; greyed on unsupported models). No Manual, no Bypass. C WQ, C PM, C DESK
CONFIRMED: defaultMode bypassPermissions and dontAsk from settings files are ignored in cloud; acceptEdits honoured. Server reviews actions in auto mode on cloud sessions. C PM
CONFIRMED: mode picked in dropdown at creation and during run; resumed in the same mode after VM reclaim. C CW
NOT documented here: whether the Bash sandbox of the local CLI is used inside the VM. Docs describe VM isolation plus proxy instead.
CONFIRMED: “Plan locally, execute in cloud” via claude --permission-mode plan, commit and push the plan, then claude --cloud. C CW

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text: UNCONFIRMED for hosted agent sessions. https://opencode.ai/docs/ (fetched 2026-11-17) describes no hosted/remote agent session; it has opencode pair (web UI via one-time local link), Docker images, and OpenCode Console/Go (model access, not session hosting). Ollama: not checked for a cloud-session feature beyond kennel-and-crypt.md. Do not claim an equivalent; self-hosting means your own VM/container.

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text:
Ticket-style prompts: problem, expected result, a command that proves it. Docs only say be specific, name files, paste errors (WQ). Proof-command part ARTICLE-ONLY.
Push local commits first. Docs CONFIRM.
Output is a branch to turn into a PR. Docs CONFIRM.
Parallel sessions each get a machine. Docs CONFIRM.
Teleport needs clean tree and pushed branch. Docs CONFIRM.
Env vars visible to everyone using the environment. Docs CONFIRM; docs go further (network secrets).
Commit as you go because idle VMs are reclaimed: docs CONFIRM reclaim; the “commit as you go” habit is ARTICLE-ONLY (files saved while paused, but not guaranteed after reclaim: inference).
Narrowest network access that works: ARTICLE-ONLY advice (docs show levels, give no recommendation).
Keep repo self-sufficient (.claude/, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md). Docs CONFIRM via “what carries over”.
Plan limits shared, five sessions about five times faster use: docs CONFIRM sharing; the multiplier is ARTICLE-ONLY.
Local beats cloud for local databases, VPN, GPU, hardware: ARTICLE-ONLY as stated; docs only say local config/tools/environment fit local or Remote Control (WQ) and hardware beyond the limits fits Remote Control.
Article figures (demo timings, 40 test reruns, 61-72 s runs) are from a fictional repo: do not cite.

title: Claude Code cloud sessions: primary-source research
text: Documented: claude --cloud, claude --teleport [id], /teleport /tp, /web-setup, /autofix-pr, /schedule, /tasks, claude -p "..." --cloud <id>, CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1, claude auth login, allow_remote_sessions, claude.ai/code, Default environment, None/Limited/Full, “Allow package managers”, “Allowed domains”, network secrets, agent proxy, GitHub proxy, Quick setup, check-tools. Not documented: beta label, GPU, VPN, data-residency, sensitive-data guidance, per-branch credentials, claude cloud.

title: Factory zone: workflow-manager facts (Snakemake, Nextflow)
text:
Read 2026-11-13. Official docs only. Snakemake: “Snakemake 9.27.1 documentation” (readthedocs /en/stable/). Nextflow: nextflow.io/docs/latest/* redirects (302) to docs.seqera.io/nextflow/*; pages show no version number, only “Copyright 2026 Seqera”. Decision fed: accuracy of quest text about dry runs, stubs, resume, local runs, pinning. Method note: pages fetched via a summarising fetch tool, not raw HTML; quotes below are as returned.



CONFIRMED: --dry-run, --dryrun, -n: “Do not execute anything, and display what would be done.” https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/executing/cli.html
CONFIRMED: -p additionally prints the shell commands; tutorial: dry run “will only show the execution plan instead of actually performing the steps.” https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorial/basics.html
CONFIRMED: --lint: “Perform linting on the given workflow … print snakemake specific suggestions to improve code quality.” (cli URL above)
UNCONFIRMED: what a dry run does NOT check (that shell commands/tools work, that env/containers resolve, that outputs get produced). Docs read do not state it. Inference only: it executes nothing, so it cannot test commands. Do not teach as doc fact.
UNCONFIRMED: whether dry run validates input file existence beyond DAG building (not stated).





CONFIRMED: flag is -stub-run, alias -stub: “Run the workflow, replacing process scripts with command stubs.” https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/cli/run
CONFIRMED: stub: block “can be defined before or after the script section”. https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/process
CONFIRMED: a stub block is NOT required: with -stub-run and no stub defined, the process script runs instead (same page). Teach “give every process a stub”, not “stub is mandatory”.
CONFIRMED: stub-run status is part of the task hash, so stub results do not satisfy a real run. https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/cache-and-resume
CONFIRMED: -resume: “Run the script using cached results. Use this to continue a run that stopped because of an error.” (run URL above)
CONFIRMED: per-task hash inputs: session ID, task name, container image, modules, Conda/Spack env, CPU arch, task inputs, eval commands (25.10+), script, referenced globals, referenced ext properties, bundled scripts, stub-run flag. (cache-and-resume URL)
CONFIRMED: task resumes only if hash matches AND outputs remain in work dir; else re-executed. Cache invalidated by changed inputs, different session ID, renamed process/calling workflow, changed container/Conda env, changed script.
CONFIRMED: input file hash = full path + last-modified timestamp + size; 'lenient' cache mode ignores timestamps (helps on NFS). A process that modifies its own inputs cannot be resumed.
CONFIRMED (doc inconsistency): Tips section says “Nextflow resumes from the previous run by default” while the body says -resume is required. Treat -resume as required; flag the page for the programmer.
CONFIRMED: nextflow lint exists: “parses and analyzes the given Nextflow scripts and config files”, usage nextflow lint [options] [paths], scans directories recursively. https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/cli/lint ; command table https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/cli





CONFIRMED (Nextflow): default executor is local: “runs tasks as processes on the machine where you launch Nextflow”; suited to “development and for small pipelines”. https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/executor
CONFIRMED (Snakemake): tutorial runs locally with snakemake --cores 1 <target>; cores must always be given; --cores: “Use at most N CPU cores/jobs in parallel.” https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorial/basics.html , cli URL above. The tutorial does not use the word “local”; no scheduler is involved in the example.
CONFIRMED (Snakemake): --local-cores only matters “in cluster/cloud mode”.





CONFIRMED (Snakemake): per-rule conda env files “highly encouraged”; per-rule container allowed (“for each rule, a (Docker) container”). https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/stable/snakefiles/deployment.html
CONFIRMED (Snakemake): freezing: platform pin file (e.g. linux-64) next to env file is tried first, falling back to the regular file; gives “exactly the same environments down to the individual package builds”; generate via snakedeploy pin-conda-envs; update pins when env file changes. Referencing a pre-existing named env “can hamper reproducibility”. Same page.
CONFIRMED (Snakemake): --use-conda: without it “the conda directive is ignored”. cli URL.
CONFIRMED (Snakemake): --containerize generates a Dockerfile/Apptainer def from per-rule conda envs (deployment URL).
CONFIRMED (Nextflow conda): pin by name in spec, e.g. bwa=0.7.15; lock files list every package and dependency, “more reproducible”, optional MD5. https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/conda
CONFIRMED (Nextflow container): “Containerizing a pipeline makes it self-contained and reproducible.”; container settable per process or in config; nextflow inspect previews containers per process. https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/container
UNCONFIRMED: any official Nextflow statement to pin container tags/digests (container page gives none; its example biocontainers/samtools has no tag). Do not claim one.
Not recorded on purpose: specific image URIs/tags/versions; look them up at the registry when needed.




Nothing executed; docs only.

title: Forest and Reef: Claude Code and OpenCode facts
text:
Question: what do official docs say about instruction files, skills, context management, plan mode and subagents in Claude Code and OpenCode? Decision it feeds: accuracy of the “Forest” and “Reef” zone content in Agent Odyssey.
Read on 2026-11-13. Local claude --version: 2.1.323. The doc pages show no “last updated” date; the version read is “live site as of 2026-11-13”. OpenCode version was not recorded and its GitHub repo was NOT read (docs site only). OpenCode docs describe some V2 behaviour (“accepted in V2”), so verify against the installed version. Note: the fetch tool summarises pages with a small model; quotes marked “…” are as returned, long pages (skills, sub-agents, permission-modes) had their last ~15% unread.



CONFIRMED User file: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (personal, all projects).
CONFIRMED Project file: ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md (team-shared via source control).
CONFIRMED Local file: ./CLAUDE.local.md, personal per-project, add to .gitignore.
CONFIRMED Org-wide managed CLAUDE.md also exists (same page, “Deploy organization-wide”).
CONFIRMED Loading: CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory and every directory above it load at launch; all are concatenated (not overriding), ordered root-down so the closest is read last.
CONFIRMED Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load on demand, once Claude reads/writes/edits a file in that subdirectory.
CONFIRMED Imports: @path/to/import syntax; imported files are expanded into context with the importing file. Import parsing skips code spans/fenced blocks (wrap @README in backticks to keep literal). Imports “don’t reduce its context cost”. Imports outside the working directory prompt for approval.
CONFIRMED /init: “Run /init to generate a starting CLAUDE.md automatically”; it analyses the codebase (build commands, test instructions, conventions); if one exists it suggests improvements instead of overwriting. CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 gives an interactive multi-phase flow.
CONFIRMED /memory: lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and memory file locations, toggles auto memory, opens files in editor.
CONFIRMED Size guidance: “target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.” Use .claude/rules/ (with paths: frontmatter) for part-of-codebase rules. A file over 4 MiB is skipped.
CONFIRMED Advisory, not enforced: “Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead.” Best-practices page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices) agrees: “CLAUDE.md is for guidelines, and Claude is allowed to decide a guideline doesn’t apply”; things that must always happen belong in hooks, deny rules or managed settings.
CONFIRMED Best-practices test for what to write: “Could it find this by reading the code? Would it actually go and look? If both are yes, leave it out.” Also /context all confirms the file loaded; /doctor prompt-audit audits instruction files.
CONFIRMED AGENTS.md: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or above (default claude-md-or-agents-md); otherwise CLAUDE.md only.
CONFIRMED Auto memory (separate from CLAUDE.md): Claude-written notes at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/; first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md load each session.





CONFIRMED Layout: a directory with required SKILL.md plus optional files. Locations: personal ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; project .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; nested <subdir>/.claude/skills/...; plugin <plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; enterprise via managed settings; --add-dir directories.
CONFIRMED Frontmatter: “All fields are optional. Only description is recommended so Claude knows when to use the skill.” name defaults to the directory name. Other fields: when_to_use, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, arguments, argument-hint, context/agent (fork to subagent), model, effort, hooks, paths, shell. description+when_to_use truncated at 1,536 chars in the listing.
CONFIRMED Invocation: default = both user (/name) and Claude (automatic, by matching description). disable-model-invocation: true = user only; user-invocable: false = Claude only.
CONFIRMED Progressive loading: “in a regular session, skill descriptions are loaded into context so Claude knows what’s available, but full skill content only loads when invoked”; body then stays in context. Recommended SKILL.md under 500 lines.
CONFIRMED Bundling: supporting files (reference.md, examples.md, scripts/helper.py) allowed; scripts are “executed, not loaded”; reference with ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}.
CONFIRMED allowed-tools: tools Claude may use without asking permission during the turn that invokes the skill; it “does not restrict which tools are available”.

CONFIRMED /init: “Guided setup for creating or updating AGENTS.md” (tui page); scans repo, may ask questions; improves an existing file in place (rules page).

CONFIRMED Custom agents: Markdown files in ~/.config/opencode/agents/<name>.md or .opencode/agents/<name>.md (frontmatter description, mode, permissions; body = system prompt), or agents key in opencode.jsonc. Built-in primary agents build and plan; subagents general and explore.
CONFIRMED Custom commands exist: .opencode/commands/*.md (commands page).




Claude Code (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window, best-practices): - CONFIRMED Context window holds “your instructions, the files it reads, its own responses, and content that never appears in your terminal”. Before you type: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP tool names and skill descriptions load. - CONFIRMED /compact “replaces the conversation with a structured summary”; accepts focus text (/compact focus on the auth bug fix). Project-root CLAUDE.md, auto memory, plan-mode plan re-injected from disk; nested CLAUDE.md and paths: rules reload on demand; up to five recently touched files re-read. - CONFIRMED Auto-compaction: “Claude Code compacts automatically as you approach the limit, so a full context window doesn’t end your session.” Threshold configurable (/autocompact 500k); per-model defaults on model-config page (not read). - CONFIRMED /clear: use between unrelated tasks; “Old conversation crowds out the files you need next and costs tokens on every message.” /clear <name> names the session left; --resume returns to it. - CONFIRMED /context: “live breakdown by category with optimization suggestions, including which CLAUDE.md and auto memory files loaded”. - CONFIRMED /rewind (or Esc Esc): roll back code/conversation, or “Summarize from here”. - CONFIRMED Degradation, as stated by docs: a longer CLAUDE.md “reduce[s] adherence”; after two failed corrections, “a third correction mostly adds to a conversation that already contains two failed attempts for Claude to keep re-reading”, so /clear and re-prompt; “a focused context gets you better answers and costs less”. The docs do NOT give a mechanism (e.g. attention dilution) beyond this. - CONFIRMED Window size: best-practices says “Most current models have a 1M-token window and compaction happens on its own, so running out is rare” and lists “manage context aggressively” as an outdated tip, while /clear between tasks is still worth doing.
OpenCode (https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/, /config/): - CONFIRMED /compact (alias /summarize): “Compact the current session.” /new (alias /clear): “Start a new session.” /undo and /redo need Git. /sessions (aliases /resume, /continue) switches sessions. - CONFIRMED Config compaction: auto on/off, keep.tokens (recent context kept), buffer (share of context window kept free before auto-compaction starts). “Automatic compaction uses the selected model’s usable input budget.” - UNCONFIRMED OpenCode has no /context equivalent in the TUI doc fetched (not listed); prune/reserved options (from older versions) not on config page. - UNCONFIRMED OpenCode docs’ stated reason why long sessions degrade; none found.




CONFIRMED Plan mode: “tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them. Claude reads files, runs shell commands to explore, and writes a plan, but does not edit your source.” Enter with Shift+Tab, /plan <prompt>, or claude --permission-mode plan; default via defaultMode: plan. Ctrl+G opens plan in editor. On approval choose auto mode or manual edit approval, or keep planning.
CONFIRMED Page’s use-case summary: “Explore before changing anything | claude --permission-mode plan | Claude Code blocks edits until you approve a plan.”
UNCONFIRMED A named four-phase “explore, plan, implement, commit” recipe in the current best-practices page. The 2026-11-13 page text does not contain it (grep for “plan mode” found none); the workflow is implied by plan mode only. The previous version of that recipe is from memory and must not be cited.
CONFIRMED Verification: best-practices lists a check Claude can run: in the prompt (“run the auth tests after, and keep going until they pass”), /goal <condition>, /code-review (fresh subagent). “ask Claude for evidence: the command it ran and its output… ‘All tests pass’ on its own tells you very little.” “the single most useful line in your CLAUDE.md is the command that runs [the test suite].”
CONFIRMED Specific prompts: “If you name the file, describe the symptom, and say what ‘fixed’ looks like up front, you usually save yourself a round of corrections later.” Example: replace “fix the login bug” with “users report login fails after the session times out. look at token refresh in src/auth/, write a failing test that reproduces it, then fix it”. Vague prompts are fine for open exploration.
CONFIRMED Course correction: Esc to interrupt; after two failed corrections /clear and rewrite the prompt.
OpenCode: CONFIRMED plan primary agent “explores and plans without editing normal project files” (agents page). No OpenCode best-practices page was read.




Claude Code (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents): “Subagents are specialized AI assistants that handle specific types of tasks.” Each “runs in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access, and independent permissions.” Use one when a side task “would flood your main conversation with search results, logs, or file contents you won’t reference again: the subagent does that work in its own context and returns only the summary.” A non-fork subagent does not see the conversation history, invoked skills or files already read. Defined as Markdown with YAML frontmatter (name, description required) in .claude/agents/ or ~/.claude/agents/. Cost caveat (best-practices): each subagent spends its own tokens and can be slower than doing it inline; a fresh reviewer helps because it has not seen your reasoning, but delegating does not itself improve the answer. CONFIRMED.
OpenCode (https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/): subagents “run with fresh context in their own child sessions”, launched via the subagent tool; they run in the background and the parent receives a report when the child goes idle. Built-ins: general (broad tools, cannot launch more subagents) and explore (read-only search). CONFIRMED.

title: Forest and Reef: Claude Code and OpenCode facts
text:
CONFIRMED User file: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (personal, all projects).
CONFIRMED Project file: ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md (team-shared via source control).
CONFIRMED Local file: ./CLAUDE.local.md, personal per-project, add to .gitignore.
CONFIRMED Org-wide managed CLAUDE.md also exists (same page, “Deploy organization-wide”).
CONFIRMED Loading: CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory and every directory above it load at launch; all are concatenated (not overriding), ordered root-down so the closest is read last.
CONFIRMED Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load on demand, once Claude reads/writes/edits a file in that subdirectory.
CONFIRMED Imports: @path/to/import syntax; imported files are expanded into context with the importing file. Import parsing skips code spans/fenced blocks (wrap @README in backticks to keep literal). Imports “don’t reduce its context cost”. Imports outside the working directory prompt for approval.
CONFIRMED /init: “Run /init to generate a starting CLAUDE.md automatically”; it analyses the codebase (build commands, test instructions, conventions); if one exists it suggests improvements instead of overwriting. CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 gives an interactive multi-phase flow.
CONFIRMED /memory: lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and memory file locations, toggles auto memory, opens files in editor.
CONFIRMED Size guidance: “target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.” Use .claude/rules/ (with paths: frontmatter) for part-of-codebase rules. A file over 4 MiB is skipped.
CONFIRMED Advisory, not enforced: “Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead.” Best-practices page (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices) agrees: “CLAUDE.md is for guidelines, and Claude is allowed to decide a guideline doesn’t apply”; things that must always happen belong in hooks, deny rules or managed settings.
CONFIRMED Best-practices test for what to write: “Could it find this by reading the code? Would it actually go and look? If both are yes, leave it out.” Also /context all confirms the file loaded; /doctor prompt-audit audits instruction files.
CONFIRMED AGENTS.md: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or above (default claude-md-or-agents-md); otherwise CLAUDE.md only.
CONFIRMED Auto memory (separate from CLAUDE.md): Claude-written notes at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/; first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md load each session.

title: Fundamentals zone: tokens, context, prompts, tools, agent vs workflow
text:
Checked 2026-11-16. Official docs only; pages fetched via a summarising fetch tool (quotes as returned, short). Docs pages show no publish date. Base: P = https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/ ; C = https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ ; A = https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/ Write the site’s own wording. Nothing here is to be pasted.



CONFIRMED: tokens are “the smallest individual units of a language model” and can be words, subwords, characters or bytes. Larger tokens are used when possible (efficiency); smaller tokens let the model handle uncommon or never-seen words. P about-claude/glossary#tokens
CONFIRMED: characters per token depends on model and language. Older models: about 3.5 English characters per token. Claude 4.7 and later (incl. Sonnet 5.5, Fable/Mythos) use a newer tokenizer giving about 30 percent more tokens for the same text. P glossary; P build-with-claude/token-counting
CONFIRMED: use the token counting endpoint with the model you plan to use. The count is an “estimate” and may differ slightly from actual use. Counting is free (rate-limited). Do not reuse counts across model generations. P token-counting
Consequence: token count is not word count; the same prompt costs different amounts on different models.
UNCONFIRMED (no official page found): letter counting, exact-string copying and “how many Gs in this read” being error-prone, and DNA/protein sequences tokenising badly (arbitrary multi-letter chunks, not one token per base). Neither the glossary nor the prompting best-practices page mentions it (grep for letter/character-count/tokeniz found nothing on the latter). It is a reasonable inference from the glossary (the model sees tokens, not characters). Phrase on the site as “models read tokens, not letters, so…” and label the DNA claim as general knowledge, or show a measured demo with the count_tokens endpoint on a real FASTA line (a demo we run ourselves is a valid source).
Practical consequence (our advice, inference): for exact counting, reverse-complement, motif position, checksums or sequence-identity tasks, have the agent run code (a script, seqkit, etc.) rather than “read” the string; verify any sequence the model retypes against the source file.





CONFIRMED: the context window is all the text the model can reference when generating, including its own response; a “working memory”, distinct from training data. P build-with-claude/context-windows
CONFIRMED (API): everything in the request counts: system prompt, every message including tool results, images and documents, tool definitions, and the output including extended thinking. P context-windows
CONFIRMED (Claude Code): context holds “your instructions, the files it reads, its own responses, and content that never appears in your terminal”. At start, before you type: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP tool names, skill descriptions (plus any output style or appended system prompt). Each file read, and tool output, then adds more. C context-window; C how-claude-code-works#the-context-window
CONFIRMED: sizes up to 1M tokens depending on model (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 4.6+, Fable, Haiku 5.5 listed), others 200k. P context-windows
CONFIRMED: official “context rot” claim, verbatim in P context-windows: “more context isn’t automatically better. As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as context rot.” Anthropic links its own article for detail: A effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents (not fetched; read before citing more than the quote above). Consequence: curating what is in context matters as much as capacity.
CONFIRMED: Claude Code compacts automatically as the limit nears, replacing history with a summary. “The summary keeps your requests and key code snippets, but detailed instructions from early in the conversation may be lost.” Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md. C how-claude-code-works#when-context-fills-up
CONFIRMED survives compaction: system prompt, project-root CLAUDE.md, auto memory, skill descriptions re-injected; up to 5 recently read/edited files re-read (a file over 5,000 tokens comes back as a path only); invoked skill bodies capped at 5,000 tokens each, 25,000 total. Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md are summarised away and reload on demand. C context-window#what-survives-compaction
CONFIRMED controls: /compact focus on X, /context (live breakdown), /clear between unrelated tasks, /autocompact <tokens>, /rewind then Summarize, subagents (own context window; only a summary returns). C context-window
CONFIRMED: if one file or tool output is so large that context refills after every summary, auto-compaction stops after a few tries with an error instead of looping. C how-claude-code-works
CONFIRMED: Claude Code warns when an MCP tool output exceeds 10,000 tokens; default cap 25,000 (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS). C mcp
Consequence for bioinformatics (inference): do not cat a large VCF/BAM-derived table or a full log into the session; ask for head, counts, or a summary script, or delegate to a subagent.
UNCONFIRMED: any official numeric threshold at which degradation starts. Do not state one.





CONFIRMED: Claude Code’s system prompt is “the instructions Claude Code sends ahead of your conversation on every request”, covering how Claude uses tools, behaves safely and formats responses. Add with --append-system-prompt, replace with --system-prompt. C glossary#system-prompt
CONFIRMED: CLAUDE.md is “loaded at the start of every session as a user message after the system prompt”, not part of the system prompt. Output-style instructions likewise. Both reach Claude as “system reminders” in the conversation. C glossary#claude-md, #system-prompt, #system-reminder
CONFIRMED: system reminders also carry the skills list, hook additionalContext, file-changed notes, commit/PR attribution lines. If Claude follows a rule you did not write (e.g. Co-Authored-By), it may come from here. C how-claude-code-works#context-claude-code-adds-on-its-own
CONFIRMED: CLAUDE.md is “context, not enforced configuration”. To block an action regardless, use a PreToolUse hook. “The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them.” Target under 200 lines per file; longer files “consume more context and reduce adherence”. C memory
CONFIRMED: AGENTS.md is read in place of CLAUDE.md when no CLAUDE.md exists in or above the working dir (v2.1.277+); if both exist, only CLAUDE.md files load unless configured. Import with @AGENTS.md from CLAUDE.md to share. C memory#agents-md
CONFIRMED: editing CLAUDE.md mid-session does not reach the running session until /clear, /compact or restart (from the prompt-caching page, via search summary; C prompt-caching not fetched directly). Re-check before stating as fact.
CONFIRMED: harness = tools, context management and execution environment around the model; Claude Code is the harness. C glossary#agentic-harness
Consequence: three layers of authority. Harness system prompt (you rarely edit) > your CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (persistent, advisory, spends context every session) > the prompt you type (this task only). Put rules that must never be broken in hooks/permissions, not prose.
UNCONFIRMED: the user-prompt vs system-prompt precedence/weighting inside the model; no official statement fetched. Do not claim system always wins.





CONFIRMED: loading every tool definition up front causes “context bloat” (a typical five-server setup “can consume ~55k tokens in definitions before Claude does any work”; tool search “typically reduces this by over 85 percent”, loading 3 to 5 tools) and a selection problem: “Claude’s ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30-50 available tools”. title: Fundamentals zone: tokens, context, prompts, tools, agent vs workflow
text:
CONFIRMED: tokens are “the smallest individual units of a language model” and can be words, subwords, characters or bytes. Larger tokens are used when possible (efficiency); smaller tokens let the model handle uncommon or never-seen words. P about-claude/glossary#tokens
CONFIRMED: characters per token depends on model and language. Older models: about 3.5 English characters per token. Claude 4.7 and later (incl. Sonnet 5.5, Fable/Mythos) use a newer tokenizer giving about 30 percent more tokens for the same text. P glossary; P build-with-claude/token-counting
CONFIRMED: use the token counting endpoint with the model you plan to use. The count is an “estimate” and may differ slightly from actual use. Counting is free (rate-limited). Do not reuse counts across model generations. P token-counting
Consequence: token count is not word count; the same prompt costs different amounts on different models.
UNCONFIRMED (no official page found): letter counting, exact-string copying and “how many Gs in this read” being error-prone, and DNA/protein sequences tokenising badly (arbitrary multi-letter chunks, not one token per base). Neither the glossary nor the prompting best-practices page mentions it (grep for letter/character-count/tokeniz found nothing on the latter). It is a reasonable inference from the glossary (the model sees tokens, not characters). Phrase on the site as “models read tokens, not letters, so…” and label the DNA claim as general knowledge, or show a measured demo with the count_tokens endpoint on a real FASTA line (a demo we run ourselves is a valid source).
Practical consequence (our advice, inference): for exact counting, reverse-complement, motif position, checksums or sequence-identity tasks, have the agent run code (a script, seqkit, etc.) rather than “read” the string; verify any sequence the model retypes against the source file.

title: Fundamentals zone: tokens, context, prompts, tools, agent vs workflow
text:
CONFIRMED: the context window is all the text the model can reference when generating, including its own response; a “working memory”, distinct from training data. P build-with-claude/context-windows
CONFIRMED (API): everything in the request counts: system prompt, every message including tool results, images and documents, tool definitions, and the output including extended thinking. P context-windows
CONFIRMED (Claude Code): context holds “your instructions, the files it reads, its own responses, and content that never appears in your terminal”. At start, before you type: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP tool names, skill descriptions (plus any output style or appended system prompt). Each file read, and tool output, then adds more. C context-window; C how-claude-code-works#the-context-window
CONFIRMED: sizes up to 1M tokens depending on model (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 4.6+, Fable, Haiku 5.5 listed), others 200k. P context-windows
CONFIRMED: official “context rot” claim, verbatim in P context-windows: “more context isn’t automatically better. As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as context rot.” Anthropic links its own article for detail: A effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents (not fetched; read before citing more than the quote above). Consequence: curating what is in context matters as much as capacity.
CONFIRMED: Claude Code compacts automatically as the limit nears, replacing history with a summary. “The summary keeps your requests and key code snippets, but detailed instructions from early in the conversation may be lost.” Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md. C how-claude-code-works#when-context-fills-up
CONFIRMED survives compaction: system prompt, project-root CLAUDE.md, auto memory, skill descriptions re-injected; up to 5 recently read/edited files re-read (a file over 5,000 tokens comes back as a path only); invoked skill bodies capped at 5,000 tokens each, 25,000 total. Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md are summarised away and reload on demand. C context-window#what-survives-compaction
CONFIRMED controls: /compact focus on X, /context (live breakdown), /clear between unrelated tasks, /autocompact <tokens>, /rewind then Summarize, subagents (own context window; only a summary returns). C context-window
CONFIRMED: if one file or tool output is so large that context refills after every summary, auto-compaction stops after a few tries with an error instead of looping. C how-claude-code-works
CONFIRMED: Claude Code warns when an MCP tool output exceeds 10,000 tokens; default cap 25,000 (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS). C mcp
Consequence for bioinformatics (inference): do not cat a large VCF/BAM-derived table or a full log into the session; ask for head, counts, or a summary script, or delegate to a subagent.
UNCONFIRMED: any official numeric threshold at which degradation starts. Do not state one.

title: Fundamentals zone: tokens, context, prompts, tools, agent vs workflow
text:
CONFIRMED: Claude Code’s system prompt is “the instructions Claude Code sends ahead of your conversation on every request”, covering how Claude uses tools, behaves safely and formats responses. Add with --append-system-prompt, replace with --system-prompt. C glossary#system-prompt
CONFIRMED: CLAUDE.md is “loaded at the start of every session as a user message after the system prompt”, not part of the system prompt. Output-style instructions likewise. Both reach Claude as “system reminders” in the conversation. C glossary#claude-md, #system-prompt, #system-reminder
CONFIRMED: system reminders also carry the skills list, hook additionalContext, file-changed notes, commit/PR attribution lines. If Claude follows a rule you did not write (e.g. Co-Authored-By), it may come from here. C how-claude-code-works#context-claude-code-adds-on-its-own
CONFIRMED: CLAUDE.md is “context, not enforced configuration”. To block an action regardless, use a PreToolUse hook. “The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them.” Target under 200 lines per file; longer files “consume more context and reduce adherence”. C memory
CONFIRMED: AGENTS.md is read in place of CLAUDE.md when no CLAUDE.md exists in or above the working dir (v2.1.277+); if both exist, only CLAUDE.md files load unless configured. Import with @AGENTS.md from CLAUDE.md to share. C memory#agents-md
CONFIRMED: editing CLAUDE.md mid-session does not reach the running session until /clear, /compact or restart (from the prompt-caching page, via search summary; C prompt-caching not fetched directly). Re-check before stating as fact.
CONFIRMED: harness = tools, context management and execution environment around the model; Claude Code is the harness. C glossary#agentic-harness
Consequence: three layers of authority. Harness system prompt (you rarely edit) > your CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (persistent, advisory, spends context every session) > the prompt you type (this task only). Put rules that must never be broken in hooks/permissions, not prose.
UNCONFIRMED: the user-prompt vs system-prompt precedence/weighting inside the model; no official statement fetched. Do not claim system always wins.

No auto-update; brew upgrade claude-code. - WinGet: winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode - npm: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code (Node 22+; do not use sudo). - Linux packages: signed apt/dnf/apk repos at downloads.claude.ai (see setup page). - WSL: open the WSL distro and run the Linux installer inside it; launch claude from the WSL terminal. WSL 2 supports sandboxing; WSL 1 and native Windows do not. - System requirements: macOS 13+, Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, Alpine 3.19+, Windows 10 1809+; 4 GB+ RAM; internet required. - Native installs auto-update in the background; claude update forces it. Free claude.ai plan has no Claude Code access. - API key (Console): export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...; in interactive mode Claude Code asks once to approve the key. Or choose the Console account at /login. - Precedence gotcha (quoted behaviour): if a subscription AND ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are both present, the key is used once approved; fix with unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, confirm with /status. - /logout to re-authenticate; claude auth login / claude auth logout exist in the shell; claude setup-token makes a one-year token for CI (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN). - Credentials: macOS Keychain; Linux ~/.claude/.credentials.json mode 0600.

Latest version. v0.40.16, 2026-11-09 (stable; gh api repos/ollama/ollama/releases/latest). v0.40.17-rc0 (2026-11-10) is a pre-release.
Install (https://github.com/ollama/ollama README; https://docs.ollama.com/linux, 2026-11-13): - macOS: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh or the .dmg from ollama.com/download/Ollama.dmg - Linux: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh. Manual: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst | sudo tar x -C /usr, then ollama serve; verify with ollama -v. Systemd unit uses ExecStart=/usr/bin/ollama serve. - Windows: irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex or OllamaSetup.exe. The Windows page serves the API on http://localhost:11434 and does not mention WSL. - WSL: no dedicated primary-source guidance found. UNCONFIRMED. Options are the Linux installer inside WSL, or Windows Ollama reached from WSL (networking not documented).
CLI (https://docs.ollama.com/cli): ollama pull <model>, ollama run <model> [prompt], ollama ls, ollama ps (running models), ollama rm <model>, ollama stop <model>, ollama serve (--help lists env vars). ollama show was not on the CLI page.
Context length (https://docs.ollama.com/context-length, 2026-11-13): - Default depends on VRAM: under 24 GiB VRAM = 4k; 24-48 GiB = 32k; 48 GiB+ = 256k. A 16 GB laptop therefore gets 4k. - Docs: web search, agents and coding tools should use “at least 64000 tokens”. - Raise: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve, or the slider in the Ollama app settings. Inside ollama run: /set parameter num_ctx 4096 (shown on https://docs.ollama.com/faq, which also says the default is 4096 and that API requests can pass "options": {"num_ctx": 4096}). The FAQ and context pages differ on the default (flat 4096 vs VRAM-tiered); the context-length page is more specific. - Check: ollama ps shows PROCESSOR (e.g. 100% GPU, or a CPU/GPU split) and, per the context page, CONTEXT. Docs advise avoiding CPU offload. More context needs more memory; a 64k context on 16 GB unified memory may cause CPU spill or slow generation (inference; not measured here).
Small tool-capable models (library pages, 2026-11-13). Capability is stated per family; per-tag tool support is not broken out, so confirm with the “tools” badge on each page. | Tag | Download | Context | Tools | Source | |—|—|—|—|—| | qwen3:8b | 5.2 GB | 40K | family tagged tools, thinking | ollama.com/library/qwen3 | | qwen3:4b | 2.5 GB | 256K | same | same | | llama3.1:8b | 4.9 GB | 128K | tools | ollama.com/library/llama3.1 | | granite4:3b | 2.1 GB | 128K | tools | ollama.com/library/granite4 | | qwen3.5:4b | 3.3-4.0 GB | 256K | family: vision, tools, thinking | ollama.com/library/qwen3.5 | | qwen3.5:9b (latest) | 6.6-7.6 GB | 256K | same | same | | gemma4:e4b | 6.6-9.5 GB | 128K | tools (family) | ollama.com/library/gemma4 | - Also in the tools-filtered listing: bonsai-2 (4b, 9b) and ornith (9b). Sizes in GB not read. UNCONFIRMED for fit. - Do not recommend qwen3-coder here: only 30b (19 GB) and 480b tags exist. - “Fits 16 GB” is my inference from file size only (KV cache and OS need extra headroom); the docs read did not state per-model RAM needs. Download size here is for the default quant listed on the page. - The Ollama OpenCode page uses qwen3.5 in its example; the OpenCode providers page uses ollama pull qwen3:8b.

title: Kennel and crypt: primary-source research
text: From primary sources: - Default 4k context on a 16 GB machine is far below the 64k that Ollama says agents need and OpenCode “requires”. Symptom is an agent that forgets instructions or tool results. Raising context costs memory and can force CPU offload (ollama ps). - Tool calling is a model capability flag; the Ollama tool-calling docs list no model guarantees. Models can return multiple tool calls per reply, and streaming needs chunk assembly. Docs hint that telling the model it is in a loop helps. - Local-model safety is the tool’s, not the model’s: OpenCode’s default policy is allow-all and “Shell is not a sandbox”; Claude Code’s rules are best-effort for reads and fragile for argument patterns. Neither stops a weak model from running a destructive command that your rules fail to match. - Claude Code sandbox leaves ~/.ssh readable and secrets in the environment by default. General (NOT backed by a primary source I read; mark as teaching opinion or test yourself): 3B-8B models are more prone to malformed tool-call JSON, looping, hallucinated flags and file paths, losing the task on long sessions, and weaker multi-file edits than hosted frontier models. Verify before stating as fact.

title: Plan mode: Claude Code and OpenCode
text:
Checked 2026-11-16. Official docs only. Fetched through a summarising fetch tool (wording is the tool’s paraphrase, not verbatim). Base: C = https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ ; O = https://opencode.ai/docs/ Not repeated: entry basics already in forest-and-reef.md s5, kennel-and-crypt.md (mode table), session-management.md (plan re-injected after compaction, Explore/Plan one-shot). Only additions below. Caveat: C permission-modes was read to char 100000 of 120324; the last ~20k chars were not read.



CONFIRMED: three entries: Shift+Tab mid-session, /plan before a prompt, claude --permission-mode plan. Default: defaultMode: plan in project .claude/settings.json.
CONFIRMED: VS Code ignores project settings for the starting mode; use claudeCode.initialPermissionMode: plan in VS Code user settings.
CONFIRMED: to leave plan mode with no prompt open, press Shift+Tab again. At the approval prompt press Esc first, because Shift+Tab there APPROVES the plan. (Teaching trap.)
CONFIRMED: status bar shows ⏸ plan mode on. C common-workflows#plan-before-editing





CONFIRMED: reads allowed; Claude may run shell commands to explore. Which shell commands run unprompted depends on the session (first match wins):

Interactive terminal with bypass permissions available: no classifier, no prompt for planning commands.
Auto mode available and useAutoModeDuringPlan on (default): the auto-mode classifier reviews shell commands, except critical-path removals.
Otherwise: commands outside the built-in read-only set prompt, even with sandbox auto-allow.

CONFIRMED: plan files are an exception to the .claude/ protected-directory rule, so they can be written in plan mode.
Source: C permission-modes





CONFIRMED: when ready, Claude presents the plan and asks how to proceed. Options (exact labels):

Yes, and use auto mode (reads Yes, auto-accept edits if auto mode is unavailable; reads Yes, and switch to BYPASS PERMISSIONS (no further prompts) for this session if the session started with bypass).
Yes, manually approve edits.
No, keep planning (you say what to change).

CONFIRMED: setting showClearContextOnPlanAccept adds a first option that approves and clears the planning context. The page does not give its label. Off by default is NOT stated; treat default as UNCONFIRMED.
CONFIRMED: approving exits plan mode and switches to the mode of the chosen option. To plan again, Shift+Tab or /plan.
CONFIRMED: Ctrl+G opens the proposed plan in the default text editor to edit before Claude proceeds.
CONFIRMED: plan files live in ~/.claude/plans/ by default; plansDirectory setting changes it.
UNCONFIRMED: whether plan context is kept when you pick a non-clear option (page says only that the clear option clears it; keeping is implied, not stated).
CONFIRMED: accepting a plan gives the session a title based on the plan, unless already named.





UNCONFIRMED: any “skip planning if the diff fits in one sentence” wording. grep of C best-practices (fetched 2026-11-16) found no “plan mode”, no “ExitPlanMode”, no such sentence. Do not cite it.
CONFIRMED (adjacent): best-practices recommends brainstorming before building: prompt Claude to interview you “until you could write the spec”, write SPEC.md, then start a FRESH session to build from it (clean context, written definition of done). This is the page’s plan-first pattern, not plan mode. C best-practices#brainstorm-with-claude-first
CONFIRMED: review against the plan: use a subagent to review the diff against SPEC.md (requirements implemented, edge cases tested). /code-review reviews the diff in a fresh subagent that never saw your conversation. C best-practices
CONFIRMED: common-workflows says use plan mode “for changes you want to review before they touch disk”. That is the only official when-to-plan line found. C common-workflows#plan-before-editing
CONFIRMED: best-practices says a vague prompt is “completely fine” when exploring, at the cost of more correction.





CONFIRMED: in an interactive terminal session with bypass permissions available, Claude is only INSTRUCTED to plan without editing; Claude Code does not enforce it, and edits or shell commands run without a prompt. Explicit ask rules and critical-path rm/rmdir still prompt.
CONFIRMED: -p (non-interactive), Agent SDK and VS Code chat panel keep plan mode’s blocks even with bypass available.
CONFIRMED: deny rules block in every mode. Hooks and mods can approve some calls (details on the permissions page, not read).
UNCONFIRMED: MCP tools in plan mode. The page does not describe MCP-specific behaviour.
UNCONFIRMED: side effects of read-only shell commands. Not discussed; teach as an inference only (“read-only set” is not a guarantee against everything).





CONFIRMED: built-in Plan subagent is a read-only research agent that Claude uses in plan mode to gather codebase context; Write and Edit denied; own context window, so the main thread stays read-only. Inherits parent model; starts WITHOUT CLAUDE.md files and git status snapshot; one-shot, no agent ID, cannot be resumed. Explore is the same but for search. C sub-agents
CONFIRMED: /rewind (aliases /undo, /checkpoint; or Esc Esc on empty prompt) tracks Claude’s file-edit-tool changes only. Bash-made changes to a file never edited by Claude are not tracked; subagent edits usually not restored; keep Git. Menu actions: Restore code and conversation / Restore conversation / Restore code / Summarize from here / Summarize up to here / Never mind. C checkpointing
UNCONFIRMED: whether /rewind covers plan files in ~/.claude/plans/. Not stated.





CONFIRMED: built-in primary agents build (default, full tools; reading .env files asks) and plan (“explores and plans without editing normal project files”; can write OpenCode plan files when asked; shell stays under permission control). Subagents general (cannot launch subagents) and explore (read-only). O agents
CONFIRMED: plan agent: cannot edit files except under the plan directory ~/.opencode/plan; edit restriction is a deny, saved approvals never override a deny. Base policy for every agent is allow-all plus ask on *.env/*.env.*. O permissions
CONFIRMED: disable plan with {"agents": {"plan": {"disabled": true}}}; default_agent picks the primary agent; falls back to build. O agents
UNCONFIRMED: how to switch between build and plan. Neither agents nor tui page mentions a Tab key or agent_cycle keybind (tui page does not mention plan at all). Do not state “press Tab”.
UNCONFIRMED: full default denies of plan beyond edit, and any plan approval step. permissions page: no plan-specific approval; ask rules answer once, always, reject. Plan is not a gate that “hands over” to build.
CONFIRMED: TUI slash commands (no /plan): /connect /compact(/summarize) /editor /exit /export /help /init /models /new(/clear) /redo /sessions(/resume,/continue) /themes /thinking /undo /update. /undo removes last message and its file changes, needs Git. O tui





Documented (Claude Code): claude --permission-mode plan, /plan [prompt], Shift+Tab, Ctrl+G, defaultMode: plan, useAutoModeDuringPlan, showClearContextOnPlanAccept, plansDirectory, ~/.claude/plans/, claudeCode.initialPermissionMode, Plan subagent, /rewind, /undo, /code-review.
Not documented / not found: a --plan flag, an “exit plan mode” slash command (only Shift+Tab), the tool name ExitPlanMode on the pages read, a plan “edit” option in the approval list (editing is Ctrl+G), a plan file name pattern, plan-mode MCP rules.
OpenCode documented: build, plan, general, explore, default_agent, agents.plan.disabled, ~/.opencode/plan. Not documented: /plan command, Tab switching, a plan approval flow.

title: Session management: fresh starts, side ideas, handoffs, parking lots
text:
Checked 2026-11-16. Official pages fetched via a summarising fetch tool (quotes as returned, short; paraphrase on the site). Not repeated here: what survives compaction table, CLAUDE.md/auto memory basics, /usage cost mechanics, “two failed corrections” quote (see fundamentals.md, failure-modes.md). Base: C = https://code.claude.com/docs/en/ ; A = https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/ ; O = https://opencode.ai/docs/ Decision fed: quest text on when to /clear vs continue, handling side ideas, handoff notes, parking lots. Slash-command names are in section 5.



CONFIRMED: /clear between unrelated tasks. “It costs nothing, and it means the next task doesn’t keep paying for the previous one’s history.” /clear oauth-migration labels the session you are leaving so you can return. C best-practices#keep-cost-and-context-down
CONFIRMED: a session with three unrelated tasks “re-reads all three on every turn of the fourth”. Best-practices table also says a focused context “gets you better answers” and costs less, even with a 1M window. C best-practices
CONFIRMED: after writing a spec, “start a fresh session to build from it, so the build begins with a clean context and a written definition of done” (SPEC.md via the interview prompt). C best-practices (spec section)
CONFIRMED: Claude Code “compacts automatically as you approach the limit, so a full context window doesn’t end your session”. Levers before it fires: /compact <focus> (example /compact focus on the auth bug fix, “before starting a long new task”), /rewind then Summarize from/up to here, /autocompact <tokens> (e.g. /autocompact 500k), /clear, delegate large reads to a subagent. C context-window#when-your-context-fills-up
CONFIRMED: /context [all] is the live fullness check: colored grid, optimisation suggestions, capacity warnings; all expands the per-item breakdown and lists loaded Memory files. C commands
CONFIRMED: idle compaction exists: with the one-hour cache, a session past about 200K tokens that sits idle “is compacted shortly before the cache expires, so after lunch you continue from a summary. If you don’t need the history at all, a fresh session still costs less.” Cache is about one hour on a subscription, five minutes on API key/cloud/credits. C best-practices (cost section), C context-window (links idleCompaction setting)
CONFIRMED: resume restores messages, model, permission mode (terminal --continue/--resume), active /goal; not --mcp-config, --plugin-dir, --add-dir, --settings, --fallback-model (pass again). If compacted, the resumed session continues from the last summary. C sessions#what-a-resumed-session-restores
CONFIRMED: “Resume this conversation?” dialog (Pro/Max/Ultra, long conversation after a long break or different model) estimates share of the 5-hour limit the saved conversation alone would use; choices Resume or Start a new conversation. “Choose by whether your next task still needs the saved conversation.” C sessions#the-resume-this-conversation-dialog
CONFIRMED: two terminals resuming the same session both write one transcript; messages can go missing. Use --fork-session on each. C sessions#branch-a-session
UNCONFIRMED: a documented context-percentage status-line field or “context fullness” signal. The statusline page was not fetched (/statusline exists, C commands). Fetch C statusline before claiming one.
UNCONFIRMED: the exact auto-compact threshold; docs defer to model-config “Default auto-compact thresholds” (not fetched).
Rule of thumb for the site (inference from the above): continue when the next step needs the same files, decisions and failed attempts; clear when the task changed, or when the transcript is mostly dead ends.





CONFIRMED subagents: “Use one when a side task would flood your main conversation with search results, logs, or file contents you won’t reference again: the subagent does that work in its own context and returns only the summary.” Built-in Explore = fast read-only agent for searching codebases. Each invocation is a new instance unless you ask Claude to resume it; Explore and Plan are one-shot and cannot be resumed. C sub-agents; C common-workflows#delegate-research-to-subagents
CONFIRMED: /btw <question> asks a side question “without adding to the conversation history”. Works while Claude is busy; sees the conversation so far; no tool access (cannot read files or run commands); single response; press f to fork it into a background subagent with full tools. Newest 20 side exchanges are replayed to later /btw. C interactive-mode#side-questions-with-btw; C commands
CONFIRMED: /branch [name] copies the conversation, switches you into the copy, original stays and is reachable by /resume. CLI form: claude --continue --fork-session. In-flight background subagents/Bash keep running and report into the branch, not the original. C sessions#branch-a-session; C commands
CONFIRMED: /subtask <task> spawns a forked background subagent that inherits the whole conversation and returns its result here; /fork [prompt] copies the conversation into a separate background session (own worktree before code edits, v2.1.221+); /background [prompt] (alias /bg) detaches the current session. C commands
CONFIRMED: you can type while Claude works; messages queue. A mid-turn message has no checkpoint of its own (“No code restore”). C interactive-mode#queue-messages-while-claude-works; C checkpointing
CONFIRMED plan mode: Claude reads and proposes, no edits until approved; claude --permission-mode plan, Shift+Tab until the bar shows plan mode, or /plan [description]. The plan Claude wrote is re-injected from disk after compaction. Accepting a plan gives the session a generated title. C common-workflows#plan-before-editing; C commands; C context-window
CONFIRMED checkpoints: every prompt that starts a turn is a checkpoint; last 100 kept. /rewind (aliases /checkpoint, /undo) or Esc Esc on empty input. Options: restore code and conversation / conversation only / code only / Summarize from here / Summarize up to here. Summarize leaves files alone and the original messages stay in the transcript. Pitch: “Exploring alternatives”. C checkpointing
CONFIRMED limits: files changed only by Bash are not tracked; subagent edits mostly not restored; external and other-session edits not tracked; symlinks/hard links skipped; “Not a replacement for version control”; snapshots swept after about 30 days. C checkpointing#limitations. Bioinformatics note (inference): sed -i or a script rewriting a results table is a Bash change, so commit first.
CONFIRMED worktrees: claude --worktree <name> or -w <name> creates .claude/worktrees/<name>/ on branch worktree-<name>; second terminal, second name = isolated parallel session. Docs suggest adding .claude/worktrees/ to .gitignore. Fresh checkout: gitignored files (.env) absent unless listed in .worktreeinclude; data directories need worktree.symlinkDirectories or a setup step. C worktrees; C best-practices
CONFIRMED: worktrees share .git, project-scope plugins, “don’t ask again” permission rules (saved to main checkout .claude/settings.local.json); auto memory is per repository, all worktrees share it; a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md exists only in the worktree where created. Exit: clean unnamed worktree auto-removed; named or dirty one prompts keep/remove. C worktrees; C memory
CONFIRMED: worktrees isolate file edits only; subagents split work inside one session; cross-session messaging lets sessions in worktrees pass findings. C worktrees (intro)
CONFIRMED naming: claude -n <name> at startup, /rename <name>, Ctrl+R in the picker. Without a name /rename auto-generates one. Resume by claude --resume <name> or /resume <name>; ambiguous name opens the picker pre-filtered. Unnamed sessions get a generated title (usable as a handle), but the default dir-xx label is not. C sessions#name-your-sessions
CONFIRMED picker (/resume or claude --resume): Space preview, Ctrl+R rename, / search (a PR URL finds its session), Ctrl+W all worktrees, Ctrl+A all projects, Ctrl+B current git branch. claude --from-pr <number> filters to a PR’s sessions. -p/SDK//loop sessions are hidden from the picker and --continue. C sessions#use-the-session-picker
CONFIRMED: /recap makes a one-line summary on demand (cap 400 characters); an automatic recap appears after 3+ minutes away (3+ turns in). Off via /config. C interactive-mode#session-recap
CONFIRMED: /clear then /resume restores the old conversation; in the same process the rewind menu has a “previous session” entry. C commands; C checkpointing
OpenCode: UNCONFIRMED for share, branch/fork. opencode.ai/docs/share returned 404 (page may live elsewhere). CONFIRMED on the TUI page: /new (alias /clear), /sessions (aliases /resume, /continue), /compact (alias /summarize), /undo and /redo (need a git repo), /export (to Markdown in your editor). CONFIRMED on config page: compaction keys auto, keep.tokens, buffer. O tui, O config. Note the TUI page itself documents only manual compaction.





CONFIRMED: “Each Claude Code session begins with a fresh context window”; CLAUDE.md and auto memory carry knowledge. Memory is “context, not enforced configuration”. C memory (detail in failure-modes.md)
CONFIRMED: asking “remember that the API tests require a local Redis instance” saves to auto memory; “add this to CLAUDE.md” writes the instruction file. Claude “decides what’s worth remembering”; it does not save every session. /memory opens, toggles, lists. C memory
CONFIRMED: CLAUDE.local.md at the project root holds private per-project preferences, “add CLAUDE.local.md to your .gitignore”. It loads after CLAUDE.md in the same directory. For sharing across worktrees, import a file from your home directory. Only official guidance found on keeping notes out of git. C memory#claude-local-md (section anchor unverified)
CONFIRMED: rules that are task-specific and not needed every session belong in skills, not CLAUDE.md. C memory (note under rules)
CONFIRMED: SessionStart hooks matching the compact source run after compaction and add output to context (a route to re-inject notes). C context-window#what-survives-compaction
CONFIRMED (Anthropic long-running agents): “getting agents to make consistent progress across multiple context windows remains an open problem”; each new session “begins with no memory of what came before”. A first “initializer agent” sets up init.sh, claude-progress.txt and an initial git commit. A: effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents
CONFIRMED: feature list feature_list.json, every feature starts failing; agents may edit “only by changing the status of a passes field”. JSON chosen because “the model is less likely to inappropriately change or overwrite JSON files compared to Markdown files”. (Summariser noted one stray reference to tests.json in the article.) A: same
CONFIRMED: coding agent works on one feature at a time, commits with descriptive messages and updates the progress file, “so bad changes can be reverted”. A: same
CONFIRMED startup routine each session: pwd; read git logs and progress file; pick the highest-priority unfinished feature; read init.sh; run a basic end-to-end test before new work. A: same
CONFIRMED failure table: declares victory too early (fix: feature list); leaves bugs or undocumented progress (git plus progress notes); marks features done prematurely (self-verify before marking passing); wastes time working out how to run the app (init.sh). A: same
CONFIRMED (Anthropic context engineering): “structured note-taking”: the agent “regularly writes notes persisted to memory outside of the context window” (examples: Claude Code to-do list, a NOTES.md); also compaction, sub-agents returning about 1,000 to 2,000 token summaries; “context rot” as recall degrades with growth. A: effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents
CONFIRMED: no official Claude Code page found that prescribes a handoff-file template or a scratch-file location. Do not present one as official.
INFERENCE, general practice (handoff note contents): goal in one line; current state (branch, last commit, what runs); decisions with reasons and rejected options; verified (command and result) versus assumed or not run; open problems and traps (e.g. a reference genome build, a sample that fails); exact next step; pointers to files, job IDs, work directories, not pasted logs. Keep it short enough that reading it costs less than rediscovery.
INFERENCE: pair the note with a commit so state is recoverable: a progress file mirrors Anthropic’s pattern, git history is the audit trail. Write the note before /clear, not after, because /clear drops the conversation.
COMMUNITY (unsourced, flag as such): ad hoc HANDOFF.md/PROGRESS.md/NOTES.md files, or asking the agent to “summarise this session into a file” before ending. The session-handoff skill in this environment is a local tool, not an Anthropic doc.
UNCONFIRMED: whether /export output suits a handoff. It is “plain text … for a person to read” (C sessions#export-and-locate-session-data); transcripts are long, so a curated note is better (inference).





No official Anthropic or OpenCode guidance found on a “parking lot” file. Treat all below as INFERENCE / general practice, not documented features.
A TODO.md/IDEAS.md (or GitHub issues) outside the agent’s current task: one line per idea, with where it came from and why it might matter. Capture, do not act. Matches the pull to “follow the shiny idea” that bloats context.
Mechanisms the docs do support for the same job: /btw for a question that needs no action (no history cost); /subtask or Explore subagent to investigate an idea while the main thread continues; /branch to try it without losing the main path; a worktree session to build it in isolation; a named session (/rename) to find it later.
Where to keep it (inference): in the repo if the team should see it; a gitignored file or CLAUDE.local.md-style local file if personal; an issue tracker for anything that outlives the week. Official docs only confirm that CLAUDE.local.md should be gitignored.
Caution (inference): a parking-lot file the agent reads every session costs context. Do not import it from CLAUDE.md; point to it only when needed.
